amelia a. kolbe 1816 - - · kolbe aged 25 in the conduit street household at the 1841 census, and the youngest of the three women there. and she married: amelia ann kolbe, at st pancras in 1854, indexed twice. the groom is not in the index this archive read and she is the only one of the three sisters who can currently be followed out of the house. from the census and the marriage index. **11 october 2026 - and a «miss a. kolbe» is giving money to her brother's missionary society, five minutes' walk from home.** *the evangelical magazine and missionary chronicle* for **1836** prints the subscription lists of the **orange street chapel auxiliary** of the london missionary society, and the **juvenile branch** carries **"miss a. kolbe"**, with a plain **"miss kolbe"** in a collector's list on the same page. **orange street chapel is off leicester square, in westminster** - the parish this family was baptised in, and a few minutes from **conduit street**, where she was living five years later. **the society is the one her brother served**: george augustus kolbe was the lms missionary at philippolis in 1836, the year of these lists. **what makes it attractive is the whole of the evidence: a surname, an initial, a parish and a society.** no address, no age, no relationship is printed, and **"kolbe" in london is not unique** - this archive has already had to keep four men of one name apart in south africa. **nothing is claimed and no record is altered.** **what would settle it** is the auxiliary's own papers rather than the printed total: the orange street chapel records, or the lms auxiliary returns in the council for world mission archive - **which is the same collection row 135 is already writing to.** **and if it is her, it says something this archive has wanted and not had:** that the family in london knew what the son at the cape was doing, and paid towards it.

andries frederick kolbe of leeuwberg 1856 - - · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 45, at leeuwberg in the bloemfontein district. tna wo 108/368 folio 431. sent to cape town and natal. leeuwberg is the farm commandant john gerson eliezar kolbe died on, on 3 april 1868, of typhus caught on commando, leaving a widow and twelve children - eight sons and four daughters, of whom this archive can put a hand on two. thirty-three years later a kolbe is still farming it. born about 1856, this man would have been twelve when the commandant died, and he sits inside the age bracket of those eight sons. the farm also carries the jephts of the 1868 horse-theft case. **27 september 2026 - the descent is now documented, and this sentence is kept so the change can be seen.** it used to read: *no descent is documented and none is claimed here - what is documented is a farm, a surname and a date.* **his own death registration names both parents.** *south africa, orange free state, civil death registration, 1902-1954*: andries frederick kolbe, **died 11 april 1918 at bloemfontein**, born **1856** in the orange free state, **son of john gerson elinger kolbe and a. j. van der merwe** - the commandant's name mangled in a way this archive has now seen five times, and his wife's reduced to initials. **so the man farming leeuwberg in 1901 was the commandant's son, farming his father's farm thirty-three years after he died on it.** **read from the index and not from the image** - the entry is a transcription, and the register page has not been opened. the paper that would settle it is vab mhg m777, the 1896 estate of the commandant's widow anna jacoba van der merwe, filed under her second husband's name mccabe, which would name all twelve children. identified, unread, in bloemfontein.

q: anna j. mary booyzen 1914 - buried 23 jan 1914, brixton - d.r. section, grave 2472 · booyzen six months old - not "0 days", which is what the index says and what this archive printed for an afternoon. the register keeps years, months and days in three columns and the 6 sits in months. hers was a bought grave, marked private. the earliest booyzen burial this archive has found at brixton, and the beginning of a family plot that would take four more over the next twenty years. 

anna jacoba kolbe of 1864 3 nov 1864, baptised bloemfontein 1 jan 1865 - - · kolbe **read the year in her name before anything else.** there is a real anna jacoba kolbe in this household, and she is this child - born **3 november 1864**, baptised at **bloemfontein on new year's day 1865**, daughter of **john g. e. kolbe and anna jacoba van der merwe** (1:1:q2hl-y1lg). **she is not the woman this archive invented on 23 september.** that was her mother, entered in an 1871 marriage index under her first husband's surname as a widow is, and briefly made into a daughter here; the register image says **weduwe** and **46**, and this girl was **six years old** at that wedding. **so the error was not an absurd one - the name really is in the family - and it was still an error**, which is the more useful shape of a mistake to keep. she is the last of the twelve to be christened; her father died on the farm leeuwberg when she was **three years and five months old**. **she married andries petrus smit**, on the free state registers' evidence, and they had a **jacobus erasmus** and an **anna jacoba** - a third woman of the name in three generations. **the marriage itself is not found** and the children are index rows. 

anna jacoba van der merwe - - - · kolbe she remarried, and her second husband is why she was hard to find. the free state archives hold her under a different surname: vab mhg m777 - "mccabe, anna jacoba. nooiensvan van der merwe. eggenote john gherson [kolbe]", 1896. widowed in 1868 with twelve children and dead twenty-eight years later as mrs mccabe. her husband's own estate is beside it - vab mhg k71, "kolbe, john gerson eleazar. eggenote anna jacoba (gebore van der merwe)", 1868. and the mccabe name is already in this archive: a rosa magdalena kolbe was baptised at bloemfontein in 1890 to frederik fortuna kolbe and maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe - a second kolbe-mccabe marriage in the same small free state world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. 20 september 2026 - it may not be one. on a geni profile, the frederik fortunata kolbe of that baptism is the commandant's own son, born 1857 at bloemfontein - so the commandant's widow married francis mccabe the landdrost about april 1871, and her son married a mccabe. mccabe died ten months later leaving "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the two households were one for eleven months, and a marriage across them afterwards is ordinary rather than remarkable. and this archive already held the other half without noticing. vab mhg c129, the 1872 estate index for francis mccabe, names his first wife as maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath - and the bloemfontein baptism of 1890 names the mother as maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe. the same four-part name, carrying mccabe as a surname: she is almost certainly his daughter by raath, named for her mother entire. so a stepbrother married a stepsister, nine years after their parents' eleven-month marriage, and mccabe's obituary had already said he left "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the one link that is from a user tree and not from a document is that her husband is the commandant's son; it is not adopted, and vab mhg c129 would settle it by naming the daughters. neither estate is read. m777 is the document that would name the twelve children. married john gerson eliezar kolbe on 3 april 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. she is the third van der merwe to marry into these families. 15 september 2026 - mccabe has a first name, a birth date and an office. he is francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now british kaffraria on 29 september 1817. his obituary in the friend says he "married his second wife about ten months since - the widow of the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", and he died suddenly of heart disease on the modder river road on 23 february 1872, aged 54, leaving "a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". so: married 3 april 1843, widowed 3 april 1868 with twelve children, married again about april 1871, widowed again fifteen months later, and dead in 1896 under his name. for about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. she was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen - the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all. 27 september 2026 - her second marriage is read from the page, and it gives her an age, a farm and her own handwriting. the free state civil marriage register, 13 july 1871, enters her as **"anna jacoba kolbe, geb: van der merwe"**, aged **46**, condition **weduwe**, occupation a dash, living at **leeuwberg (bloemf.)** - the farm her husband died on, and the first record to place her there rather than at springfield. francis mccabe is entered opposite her as **53, weduwnaar, landdrost**, of bloemfontein. married by **licentie** rather than by banns, entry 874, by **gustav radloff v.d.m.** in the church of the nederduitsch gereformeerde gemeente at bloemfontein. an age of 46 in july 1871 puts her birth about 1825, which is the first indication of it this archive has had from a document. and she signed it herself - *a. jacoba kolbe geboren van der merwe* - the only specimen of her hand here, and she wrote her first husband's name before her own. this is also the document that withdraws a person this archive invented: an "anna jacoba kolbe" was briefly entered here as a daughter, and the word **weduwe** in the register's own hand says she is this woman.

david schalk booysen 9 jun 1848, cradock - after nov 1905 · booyzen prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 54 against a birth of 9 june 1848, which would have made him 52 and six days short of 53 when the ship sailed. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. if it is him, he was a transvaal burgher in arms at fifty-two, taken and deported, and he came back - he remarried at pretoria in november 1905. fourth on the 1863 list, and the direct ancestor's brother - willem hermanus is sixth on the same list. for the whole of this project he was a line on that list and nothing else. his wife's 1900 death notice gives him a household: married elizabetha margaretha marais at lady grey, the same small cape church where his brother married kathleen barry in 1879; eight children; and by 1900 he was at pretoria, living in a zinc building in market street. he signed her notice there in march 1904 - and on 27 november 1905 he married again at pretoria, to johanna elena stols, widow lowies, of skinners court. he was 56, a widower of goede hoop, pretoria, and the register gives his birthplace as cradock. the remarks column cites his remarriage certificate from the master, no. 4795 - which is the number of his first wife's death notice, so the two documents point at each other and the identification needs no inference. his own death is still not found.

s: 29 Sep 1817, a military post in what became British Kaffraria – 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein · Kolbe
q: francis mccabe 29 sep 1817, a military post in what became british kaffraria - 23 feb 1872, the modder river road, district bloemfontein · kolbe the second husband, and the reason the commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the free state estate index. landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier; his mother rose died at bloemfontein on 1 august 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. he married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 - "his second wife, about ten months since" - and was dead within fifteen months. on the anniversary of the state's independence he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the diamond fields meaning to sleep at his own farm "uitvlugt" on the modder river; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of g.f. enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. he was dead of heart disease that evening. he left four sons and two daughters of his own and "a large family of step-children", which is a newspaper counting the commandant's twelve. his brother joseph, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in december 1865; his brother john died at bloemfontein in 1860. he was buried on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 september, from the free state estate index. vab mhg c129: "mccabe, francis. eggenotes 1) maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath en 2) anna (gebore van der merwe)", 1872 - so he had a first wife and she has a name. and vab 1/3/1/12 bc11: "mccabe, francis. insolvente boedel", with the remark "bevat geen sterfkennis nie" - contains no death notice. the landdrost of bloemfontein, buried with the state president walking behind him and two hundred people after that, left an insolvent estate. his widow's own entry, m777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper. 27 september 2026 - the marriage register confirms the office and the condition, and fixes the date. the free state civil marriage entry of **13 july 1871** - not "about april", which was a tree's guess - enters him as **francis mccabe, 53, weduwnaar, landdrost**, of bloemfontein. **weduwnaar** is the register agreeing with vab mhg c129, which names a first wife: he had been widowed before he married the commandant's widow. an age of 53 in july 1871 agrees with the birth date of 29 september 1817 to within three months, from a different document. he signed his own name. he had **seven months and ten days** left.

"petition of frederick fortunatus werdmuller of malmesbury", cape supreme court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. this archive has already followed frederik fortunatus from kolbe (1839) to barry (1863) to booysen (1899); here it is again, on a werdmuller - and augusta louisa kolbe married a werdmuller. 17 september 2026 - he is shown to be her son, and the sentence above is withdrawn. the last 214 images of the burgersdorp baptism register hold his font: fredrik fortunatus steenkamp werdmuller, born 25 april 1861, baptised 19 may 1861 at burgersdorp, father coenraad johannes otto werdmuller, mother augusta louisa kolbe - familysearch 1:1:6fw6-wxgs, image 673. the settler's fourth daughter gave her child her brother's name, which is how frederik fortunatus reached a fourth surname. and it dates augusta louisa: she was bearing her husband's children in 1861, thirteen years before he married again at burgersdorp in 1874 - which bears directly on whether charles andrew was her son. the one step not taken: that the child of 1861 is the man of the 1907 petition and the 1953 estate. both are frederick fortunatus werdmuller at the cape and the name is rare; the 1907 man is of malmesbury and the child was baptised at burgersdorp, and no document read here joins them. 

frederick kolbe of 1816 bapt. 16 dec 1816, westminster - - · kolbe right surname, right parish, right decade, and a gap in the family's own baptism run exactly there. he is not a brother. his father is george and his mother elizabeth, and his register batch is c72301-7 rather than the family's c15051-2 or c06236-1. he was one click from being made an eighth son, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. the same check threw out henry kolbe, baptised at southwark on 2 february 1800 - father henry, mother susannah. and the rejection turned out not to be a dead end. morning advertiser, 31 december 1832: "left his home, monday, december 10, frederick kolbe, about 16, dark hair and eyes, with an impediment in his sight. any information addressed mrs. kolbe, no. 18, gerrard-street, soho, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…" - and a boy "about 16" in december 1832 is one baptised in december 1816. gerrard street is two streets from church street. there were two kolbe households in soho at once, and every soho kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. whether the two families were related is not known here. 

s: 1891, Wakkerstroom — about May, counting back his age at death – 2 Nov 1918, Villieria, a portion of Kleinfontein, district Wakkerstroom — aged 27 · Kolbe
q: frederik fortunatus downing kolbe 1891, wakkerstroom - about may, counting back his age at death - 2 nov 1918, villieria, a portion of kleinfontein, district wakkerstroom - aged 27 · kolbe the man who proved the convergence. he carries both of this family's kolbe names at once - frederik fortunatus off his grandfather, downing off a london marriage of 1819 - and a london surname has no business in the eastern transvaal except through that wedding. born seventy-two years after it. married hester gerbina susanna joubert at volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as "daomig". dead at wakkerstroom on 2 november 1918, four months after his brother daniel, which is the influenza. 9 october 2026 - his death notice is read, and it names his parents in his own file. tab mhg 40293, the document this archive has called its biggest single gap, is filmed and free: the sterfkennis gives vader george augustus kolbe and moeder martha sofia kolbe, geboren klopper. until today that parentage rested on his brother daniel's death registration reading "g a kolbe's son" and on his sister maria johanna's 1953 estate file; now it is stated on his own. and it decides which george augustus, which is the whole difficulty at wakkerstroom - two men of that name are buried in one cemetery, and only one of them married a klopper. the form adds what no index carried: he was a veeboer, his ordinary residence and the place he died was villieria, a portion of kleinfontein in the district of wakkerstroom, he was married in community of property, the marriage was at volksrust, and he was twenty-seven years and six months old - which puts the birth at about may 1891, where this archive had only the year. he left movables, fixed property, an estate worth more than £300 and a will. the index was wrong about where he died and this archive was right. familysearch standardises the place to "wakkerstroom, zoutpansberg, transvaal" and renders it villieria, pretoria; wakkerstroom is nowhere near zoutpansberg, and villieria here is a farm portion, not the pretoria suburb of that name. the reading that was published on 9 october said the image was not yet read and attributed pretoria to the index. it is a reason the hedge is written every time. 

s: 1839, Bethulie, Orange Free State – 23 Nov 1929, Utrecht, Natal — aged about 90 · Kolbe
q: frederik fortunatus kolbe 1839, bethulie, orange free state - 23 nov 1929, utrecht, natal - aged about 90 · kolbe the source of the fortunatus name across three families - and, as of 14 september 2026, a man with a household. the settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the orange river. he married elizabeth johanna du toit, and eight of their children are in the dutch reformed registers: baptised at colesberg in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at hopetown in 1870, and at bethulie in 1881. the eldest is a george augustus, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. then the household goes north: three of those children marry or die at wakkerstroom in the eastern transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. that is the second proof of the wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name - it is a family moving. 17 september 2026 - he has a death, a district and an estate. pietermaritzburg estate files: "frederick fortunabis kolbe, born 1839 kaap provinsie, died 23 november 1929 at utrecht", probate 1929 - familysearch 1:1:qlr2-xfjc. ninety years old. and the estate names his children, the daughters under both surnames, which is how a daughter gets followed: george augustus, gabriel stephanus, martha angelina, margaret harriet kolbe van der spuy, frederick fortunatus, catharina maria louisa kolbe louw, elizabeth johanna kolbe pattison, petronella jacoba adriana kolbe beukes and adriana henrietta johanna kolbe oosthuizen. nine, not eight - the note above is careful and says eight are in the registers; the ninth is not. the file itself is not read. 

s: 22 Oct 1859, or 1857 — two documents disagree – 18 Dec 1930, Bloemspruit, district Bloemfontein · Kolbe
q: frederik fortunatus kolbe of bloemspruit 22 oct 1859, or 1857 - two documents disagree - 18 dec 1930, bloemspruit, district bloemfontein · kolbe the fourth man of the name, and the one this archive kept meeting without entering. he is the frederik fortuna kolbe who fathered rosa magdalena, baptised at bloemfontein on 6 july 1890, and magdalena jacoba, by maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe - the second of the two kolbe-mccabe marriages. **his death is documented twice and the two documents disagree about when he was born.** the **civil death registration** - national archives of south africa, dewetsdorp death records 1930, image 852 of 2,140, familysearch 1:1:81zn-kw6z - is a *form of information of a death* completed at his death and registered the next day by the district registrar **j. s. kruger**: **age 73**, born in the **orange free state**, a **boer**, a **weduwnaar**, died **18 december 1930** at **bloemspruit** in the district of bloemfontein, to be buried at bloemfontein. cause of death, in the doctor's english inside an afrikaans form: **valvular disease of the heart, bronchial asthma, nephritis and enlarged prostate**, attended by **dr j. m. de kock**. **his gravestone says something else.** billiongraves photographed it at the **bloemfontein memoriam road cemetery** on 30 september 2018: **born 22 october 1859, died 8 december 1930**. **age 73 on 18 december 1930 means born about 1857; the stone makes him 71.** neither is a baptism, and both are at one remove - an age is what an informant said, and a stone is cut after the fact by somebody working from a family memory. **the stone's photograph is behind a paywall**, so its transcription has not been checked against the cutting, and the ten-day gap between the two death dates may be nothing more than a volunteer dropping a "1" from "18". **the bloemfontein or fauresmith baptism register would end it** and he is not in the index. **what he was to the family:** he took church membership at bloemfontein on **6 may 1882**, and he was a widower when he died, so his wife went first. **the informant at his death was a pienaar** - the signature reads **w. j. pienaar**, of **77 st john's road, bloemfontein** - and the commandant's eldest daughter catharina wilhelmina married johannes petrus pienaar at bloemfontein on 8 october 1860. **a nephew reporting his uncle's death would look exactly like this, and pienaar is one of the commonest surnames in that district.** it is written down because it is suggestive, and it is not adopted.

g.a. kolbe of piet retief 23 feb 1836 - 7 jan 1913, piet retief · kolbe a date for the twin, if it is him. the stone at piet retief reads "vader en moeder - g.a. kolbe - geb. 23 feb. 1836 - overl. 7 jan. 1913 - a.m. kolbe - geb. 4 mei 1843 - overl. 21 sep. 1907 - van hun kinders". the settler's ninth and tenth children were twins born at burgersdorp in 1836, charlotte felicia and george augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. a g.a. kolbe born 23 february 1836 is exactly the right man in exactly the right year - and it would date his twin sister too. it is initials and a year, not a name and a parent, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. it would also give the other george augustus kolbe - born burgersdorp 2 october 1861, dead standerton 1934, buried wakkerstroom - a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern transvaal kolbes have been missing.

s: 7 Dec 1802, Soho — baptised 2 Feb 1803, Westminster – 1 Dec 1844, “Wurtemburg”, Colesberg · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe 7 dec 1802, soho - baptised 2 feb 1803, westminster - 1 dec 1844, "wurtemburg", colesberg · kolbe his obituary is found, eighteen days after the death: grahamstown journal, 19 december 1844. "died at his farm, wirtemberg, near the orange river, december 1st, the rev. george augustus kolbe, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. he was the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq. of brunswick-square, london, has left a widow and ten children... he having been for many years engaged in rendering them medical advice and assistance whenever called upon... his disease was an affection on the lungs." eight sons, seven of them dead before december 1844 and not one in this archive. brunswick square, which is not conduit street and is a mile and a half from it. a man who doctored a district for thirty years, where his own death notice says only "agriculturist". and a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. the notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living - it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 settler - the nautilus, owen's party, algoa bay 14 apr 1820. married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood, and the roll carries a second one: "kolbe, george augustus 20. chemist. w margaret 19", where he was sixteen and she was sixteen. he sailed from gravesend four days before his seventeenth birthday. the two lies do not even agree - nobody "twenty-one and upwards" in january 1819 is twenty in december. owen's party was 52 people, no. 3 on the colonial department list, joint-stock and recruited in london, and it collapsed in 1821 when thomas owen refused to draw rations and left; his brother took over and the party dispersed. he was eighteen, with no leader, no rations and no location, and the next record of him is the graaff-reinet mission three years later. preached across the orange river. his grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 september - he was an lms missionary, and his father wrote to him. the south african library at cape town holds msb751, the ga kolbe collection, donated by dr jean griffiths of somerset west in 1985: "george augustus kolbe, pharmacist, 1820 settler, missionary, married margaret downing" and, on a second entry, "george augustus kolbe, 1802-44. lms missionary." it corroborates a memory this archive published the same morning as an inference - john montgomery's recollection of a bushman mission school at koolskop about 1824, where colesberg now stands. two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. the collection is four photocopied pages containing a letter of 23 august 1830 from johan kolbe in london to his son - the only known document connecting the tailor of conduit street to the settler of colesberg. it has now been read, and it does not carry a street address. the catalogue called it a letter "on his ordination" and this archive repeated the catalogue; it is not. 20 september 2026 - and a second attachment came with it. a two-page afrikaans typescript headed "msb 751 / [konsep] vir dsab / voorlopige teks", initialled ks and dated 18/2/92 - a draft entry for the dictionary of south african biography, by dr karel schoeman, on the word of the national library that holds the file: "the author, ks, would be dr. karel schoeman who worked here at the national library". it is a secondary work and this archive does not take secondary works as evidence - but it agrees with this archive on nine points reached by nine other roads (the 1802 birth, j.g.e. kolbe 1822-68 at leeuberg as a commandant, margaret downing 1803-1867, the 1819 london marriage, the apothecary's trade, the farm wurthemberg, ten children, philippolis from march 1831) and it is wrong about exactly one thing: it calls his father a german apothecary. he was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters' lists, three gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son's sworn deposition. the trade is the son's, moved one generation up. what the entry adds, all of it untested: the graaff-reinet missionary society from about 1824, working among the slaves of the district; acceptance as an lms mission assistant on 8 february 1828 and posting to boesmanskool - the present bethulie - with james clark among the san; a journey with melvill to the caledon valley in november 1828, as far as present-day ladybrand, the earliest journey in the present free state of which a written record survives, and printed under his own name in the transactions of the missionary society for 1829 - a second document he wrote himself, searched for and not found; philippolis from march 1831, alone after melvill left in march 1832; ordination on 25 may 1833 by the french missionaries arbousset and casalis; his advice behind the berlin missionary society's founding of bethanie in 1834; an accusation of adultery in 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by h. hendricks, secretary of the griqua council - an inquiry by the french missionaries acquitted him - continued opposition from t. atkinson, withdrawal from the station in march 1837 and dismissal by the lms on 19 june 1837; and the farm driefontein near philippolis. it is also wrong a second time, and in its own first source: it says his death notice records only eight children. the death notice names ten, and this archive has read it, photographed it and published the transcription - kab mooc 6/9/35: 7698, signed m. kolbe at colesberg in january 1845. it also settles the farm name. this archive had wirtemberg from the obituary and knapdaar from the death notice and had quietly run them into one address; "wurthemberg, sometimes also given as knapdaar" is the statement that assumption needed. and it names a portrait: a likeness of him as a young man, in 1992 with c.j. du plessis of ruigtevlei, district bethulie, reproduced in olivier (1973); and a charles bell watercolour of a church service at philippolis in 1834 with kolbe in the pulpit, in the africana museum, johannesburg. this archive holds no likeness of anybody born before 1850. there may be two of this man. and he wrote something else, and it is findable. the 1829 journal extract the dsab cites is catalogued under the other man's name, which is why a search for kolbe found nothing: "extracts of the journal of messrs melvill and kolbe, addressed to the rev. richard miles, superintendent of the society's missions in africa, philippolis, 25 nov. 1828", in the council for world missions archive at soas - which is source 4 on the dsab's own list, two lines above source 6. an edited version dated 18 november 1828 appears in melvill (1829), and the journey is printed entire in karel schoeman (ed.), early white travellers in the transgariep, 1819-1840 (protea, 2003), p. 30. **and a sworn witness puts him at bethulie with the bushmen, in june 1831.** *basutoland records* (1883), the cape's printed compilation of official documents, carries at **page 436** the deposition of **frans johannes cornelis cronje**, taken at **smithfield on 14 september 1858** before **johannes jacobus sauer, landdrost of the caledon river district**. cronje had come up from colesberg to hunt in **june 1831** with piet venter, barend venter, willem venter, his brother stephanus cronje and **hendrik weber, the commandant of the district**: **"we then met with the missionaries kolbe and klerk with some bushmen at bethulie."** **"klerk" is almost certainly james clark**, the man sibree pairs him with at the bushman station - a dutch deponent writing an english surname down as he heard it - and **the pairing is what identifies the kolbe.** this is **an eyewitness, under oath, naming him at work**, and it is the earliest independent sighting of him this archive holds. **it also sits awkwardly with the chronology and is not smoothed over.** sibree has him reaching **philippolis on 13 march 1831**, and schoeman's chronology says march 1831 too, so by that june he should have been a long ride away. **either he was back at his old station, or a man deposing twenty-seven years later has slipped a year** - and nothing here decides which. **and the document has an interest.** these depositions were taken to argue that the land had been empty, so the party's "no other native tribes besides a few bushmen" is testimony with a purpose and is read as such. **the page was read as an image, which corrected the transcript twice: the text file gives "barend teater" and "bethulle" where the type says barend venter and bethulie.** **11 october, late - his own journal is in print, it is free, and it has been since 1833.** the london missionary society's own monthly, *the evangelical magazine and missionary chronicle*, is on the internet archive **unrestricted, volume by volume, 1828 to 1837** - the whole of his mission. ten volumes were taken and read. **the sum of his own words in this archive was one sentence, quoted at second hand. it is now eleven months of a journal and two letters.** **the journal.** *evangelical magazine and missionary chronicle*, **1833, pp. 410-412**: **"extracts from the journal of mr. george augustus kolbe, from 8th october, 1831, to 3rd september, 1832."** philippolis, day by day. **6 november 1831**, 260 at the services, three admitted as members, the lord's supper to fifteen, and at ten at night he can still hear praying and singing. **9 november**, the chief writes to veld-cornet joubert complaining that colonists have insulted and beaten his people. **18 january 1832**, **"vaccinated twenty-six persons"** and ninety children in the school. **29 january**, a day of thanksgiving for deliverance from small-pox. **5 february**, two elders and two deacons chosen, and he sets out the church's discipline in his own hand. **15 february**, bushmen take two heifers, the thieves are whipped and the rest sent away with meat, and he writes: **"there is no need of discharging a gun, much less of shooting them."** **1 april**, the new church opens - **built entirely by the inhabitants of the district**, the society giving 200 rix-dollars and some nails and hinges; stone walls two and a half feet thick and twelve feet high, room for five hundred, and a hundred left standing in the street. **2 april, 335 children in the school.** **8 may**, he rides out to a horde of corannas with the small-pox. **23 may**, having preached against the brandy the colonists bring in, the chief prohibits its sale at the station; three days later a griqua is given so much brandy by a colonist that he is found dead in his bed. **21 july**, **"the veld-cornet joubert … and two other farmers, arrived here this afternoon, for the purpose of obtaining medical advice"** - which is the obituary's «rendering them medical advice and assistance whenever called upon», **sixteen years before the obituary, in his own journal.** **5 august**, the chapel «literally crammed», five hundred present, captain waterboer and his council down from griqua town. **the letter that settles the date this archive could not settle.** same serial, **1831**: **"extracts of a letter from rev. g. a. kolbe, dated philippolis, april 30, 1831, addressed to the foreign secretary."** it opens: **"as i resided for nearly three years among the bushmen previous to my removal to this station …"** and then says it outright - **"when i arrived, in april, 1828, with my colleague, in the bushman country."** **and his colleague says the same thing from the other side.** the 1830 volume prints a letter from **mr james clark, dated bushman station, near caledon river, 31 december 1828**: landdrost stockenstrom of graaff-reinet and the lieutenant-governor asked him to begin a new station east of philippolis near the caledon, and **"brother kolbe and myself removed to this station, and arrived here in the beginning of may last."** **two men, writing three years apart and neither for the record, put him at the bushman station in april or may 1828.** so **the dsab's 1828 is right and sibree's 8 february 1829 is not an arrival at all** - it is the society formally accepting a man who had already been in the field a year, which is exactly the reading schoeman's chronology suggested this morning and which is now **his own word and his colleague's** instead of an inference. **the conflict this archive has carried since september is closed.** **it also dates bethulie.** the station clark describes founding with him, at stockenstrom's request and with farmers' subscribed cattle, is the boesmanskool that became **bethulie**. **and it is the first time this archive has heard him on the people he worked among.** in the same 1831 letter: the bushmen's raids on the farmers' herds **"proceeded from a recollection of former injuries, excited by the intrusion of the colonists into their country"**; and **"truly, the oppression of the bushmen has been great; they have been looked upon, by many, little above the level of the brute creation; and having been subjected to a temporary slavery, they have smarted under the lash of the oppressor."** he also writes that not one of them had been brought to the faith, that **"temporal advantages are all they desire"**, and that revenge and disobedience are reckoned virtues among them - **the condescension and the indictment in one paragraph, and both are left standing here, because quoting only the half that reads well in 2026 would be choosing his words for him.** legassick quotes him: on the caledon they met people with "no other means of subsistence than the wild animals found in these parts". the first words of his this archive has read, and they are about famine. and the man he addressed it to is very probably the man who called at his father's house: richard miles was sent to cape town to act as dr philip's substitute while philip was in england, which puts him at the cape in 1828 and back in london by 1830. the 1830 letter says only "mr miles", so this is an identification and not a document. 20 september, later - and the society's own register has him, free, in eight lines. james sibree, a register of missionaries (lms, 4th ed. 1923), entry 278: "was previously connected with the graaff reinet missionary society, and laboured among the slaves around graaff reinet. was accepted provisionally by mr. miles, feb. 8, 1829, which action was confirmed by the directors, july 29, 1829. first laboured with mr. clark, at the bushman station, caledon river. thence proceeded to philippolis, arriving there, march 13, 1831. on may 26, 1833, he was ordained by the french missionaries, messrs. lemue, pellisier, and arbousset. his connection was dissolved by the directors, june 19, 1837." it settles mr miles - the man who called at the tailor's house in london was no messenger, he was the officer who accepted him - and it explains the father's adverb, because "provisionally" by miles and "confirmed" by the directors is precisely what "fully accepted" means. it disagrees with the dsab on the year of acceptance (1829, not 1828), the day of the ordination (26 may) and the men who performed it (lemue, pellissier and arbousset - no casalis). and it is wrong about a son. entry 522 calls frederick william kolbe, the rhenish then lms missionary of george and paarl, "son of rev. g. a. kolbe (no. 278)", where schoeman says he was no relation. schoeman is right and the society's own register is wrong: the arithmetic gave it away - a birth of 3 november 1821 against john gerson eliezar's 7 july 1822, eight months apart - and three works settled it. the new catholic encyclopedia calls his son monsignor f.c. kolbe "the son of a westphalian (german) protestant missionary"; s2a3 names him friedrich wilhelm kolbe, herero scholar, married at cape town in 1849 and at okahandja by april 1850; and the dsab had published its own entry on him in 1987. sibree has two kolbes in south africa and a compiler joined them. **and the dictionary itself now says so, with a town.** read 11 october 2026 by search-inside, which opens a borrowable scan without borrowing it: **dictionary of south african biography v, 419 - *kolbe, friedrich wilhelm*, born gutersloh in westphalia on 3 november 1821, died cape town 1899, a missionary and herero scholar.** the arithmetic above stands and no longer has to carry the argument alone: **a man born in westphalia in 1821 is not the son of a settler who had been at the cape since april 1820.** **his parents are still not read** - the dictionary names parents in a fixed form, and that sentence falls outside every snippet the preview allows. **and the same index says what is not there:** its cumulative list at p.922 carries **f. c. kolbe at i, 433** and the two above at **v, 419**, and **no george augustus kolbe anywhere in five volumes** - which is what this archive had already reasoned about the draft, now with the printed index agreeing. **and the son's entry finishes it.** *dictionary of south african biography* **i, 433** - **friedrich carl (frederick charles) kolbe**, the monsignor, born **george, 28 september 1854**, died **sea point, cape town, 12 january 1936** - **"was the son of friedrich wilhelm kolbe of gutersloh in westphalia, who came to south africa in 1844** as one of the earliest missionaries of the rhenish mission society in **damaraland**, and his wife, **isabella elliott**". **the settler died at colesberg on 1 december 1844.** so the man sibree made his son reached this country, aged twenty-three, from westphalia, for a different society and a different field, **in the year the settler died**. two volumes of the dictionary give the westphalian birth independently, and neither has ever joined the two families. **f. w. kolbe's own parents remain unread**, which is all that is left of that question. and his own journals are catalogued, in london. the council for world mission archive at soas, item-level: cwm/lms/05/05/100 - "extracts from the journal of john melvill and george augustus kolbe, during a tour to the north-eastwards of philippolis, 13-22 nov 1828", the manuscript behind the printed extract this archive hunted all morning; /102, extracts at philippolis 1828-1831; /106, journal, philippolis 1831-1834; /108, journal, philippolis 6 oct 1832 - sep 1833. six years of his life in his own writing. until 11 october 2026 this archive held one sentence of his at second hand; it now holds eleven months of his journal and two of his letters, printed by the society in its own monthly and free - but printed as extracts, visibly cut, so the manuscripts behind them are still the ask. and the year of the accusation is one box: incoming correspondence /044 (1835, which the catalogue says contains him), /046 (1836) and the 1837 file - 1836-1837 is box 15. and one likeness is catalogued, in scotland: university of edinburgh, centre for the study of world christianity, cswc 60 - five photograph copies of bell sketches of african congregations, item 3 "mr. kolbe… at philippolis in 1834". edinburgh calls him "a moravian missionary?", question mark and all; he was london missionary society, and this archive has his father's letter saying so. the dsab puts the original watercolour in johannesburg and never mentions scotland; edinburgh never mentions johannesburg. **11 october - schoeman published the documents behind his own draft, and they name a third man in the charge.** everything above about 1836 rests on his *voorlopige teks* of february 1992, which this archive has always labelled a secondary work it does not take as evidence. the same scholar then edited **"griqua records: the philippolis captaincy, 1825-1861"** for the **van riebeeck society, second series 25 (cape town, 1996), isbn 0958411212**, which prints the captaincy's own papers - including those of h. hendricks, who led the agitation. **its index puts g.a. kolbe on three pages**, and all three have now been read through the internet archive's search-inside, which gives page numbers and their text on a borrowable book without borrowing it. **page 35 is a contemporary document and not a gloss:** the griquas complain of **their late missionary kolbe**, whom they, with **wright and atkinson**, hold dangerous to peace and good order, and they claim the right to make him quit their territory. schoeman's footnote to it has him incurring the enmity of **hendrik hendrickze** - the book's own spelling, which its index says is discussed at p. xiii - **accused of adultery**, with **his colleagues wright and atkinson particularly zealous in pressing the charges**, gone from the station but still living north of the orange. **the draft named hendricks and atkinson; the documents add peter wright of griquatown.** the same index gives the eleven missionaries who served philippolis - **atkinson, christie, clark, kolbe, melvill, philip, schreiner, solomon, thomson, van der schalk and wright** - so two of the eleven pressed the charge against a third. **and its chronology may dissolve a disagreement this archive has carried since september.** it dates the founding of the bushman school, later bethulie, by **james clark and g.a. kolbe to may 1828**; his own arrival at philippolis to **march 1831**; theophilus atkinson's to **august 1836**; and his withdrawal to **march 1837**. if he was founding the school in may 1828 he was in the field before the society formally took him on, and **sibree's 8 february 1829 and the dsab's 8 february 1828 are then dating two different things** - the acceptance and the posting - rather than contradicting one another. **that is a reading of a chronology and not a document, and it is offered as one.** three pages is where the index has him by name: page 35 calls him "their late missionary" without the surname, which is exactly what an index cannot catch, **so the volume is not finished with.** a second kolbe in the same book is not him: the index carries **kolbe, j.** at p. 130, a lessee of a farm owed rds1480 under a settlement of sir harry smith's, printed in dutch there and in english at p. 268. **nothing is claimed about him**, and he is written down so that the next reader does not fold two initials into one man. 

george augustus kolbe of 1845 30 sep 1845, baptised colesberg 8 mar 1846 - - · kolbe the commandant's eldest son, and he carries the settler's name entire. baptised at **colesberg on 8 march 1846**, born **30 september 1845**, son of **johan gerson eliezer kolbe and anna jacoba van der merwe** - *south africa, dutch reformed church registers (cape town archives)*, familysearch 1:1:6245-2s2x. **the same event is in the index twice**, as "george augustus kolbee", baptised 15 march 1846 with the identical birth date and the same two parents (1:1:6p21-c67z) - one font, two transcriptions, a week apart, which is a warning about counting index rows and not a second child. **he was born two and a half years after his parents married** on 3 april 1843, and named for the grandfather who had died at colesberg the year before he was born - the 1820 settler, whose own death notice was signed in that town in january 1845. **what is probably his and is not adopted:** a george augustus kolbe born 1846 married **hester jacoba jacomina louw** in the free state on 15 september 1873, and an estate was filed at bloemfontein in 1905 for a george augustus kolbe born 1846 at colesburg, died 29 april 1905. **the year in both is the baptism year, not the birth year**, which is how a register-derived record usually differs from a font - but this archive holds five men of this name and will not join them on a coincidence of year. **the estate is not ordered.** 

george augustus kolbe of 1914 2 jul 1914 - - · kolbe a minor in 1919, and the fourth george augustus kolbe in this archive. his father's death notice names him as the only child: "george augustus kolbe. minderjarig, geboren 2 julie 1914." he was four when his father died and he carries his grandfather's name entire, which is what this family does - the same grandfather who outlived the father by thirty-six years. his parents' will was written five weeks before he was born, on 30 may 1914, and provides for them dying without a child; by the time it was read in 1919 he was its heir, taking the immovable property in equal shares with his mother, she holding usufruct over his portion for life. nothing is known of him after 1919. born more than a century ago and so published in full under the estate's eighty-year rule; no death, no marriage and no descendants are claimed, because none has been read. 

george augustus kolbe of bethulie 1869 - - · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 32, at sterkfontein in the bethulie district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 581. sent to natal. the second man of that name in the same list - the first being george augustus kolbe of burgersdorp, whom this archive identified from the wakkerstroom stones. bethulie is on the orange river, in the country the settler preached across. and thirteen years later a g. a. kolbe of bethulie is president of the orange free state agricultural association. the british press, 26 june to 22 july 1914: "mr. g. a. kolbe (bethulie)" in the delegate list printed by the daily telegraph; "mr g. a. kolbe, president of the orange free state agricultural association and chairman of the orange free state delegation" at the royal agricultural society's show, in the western daily press, dundee courier, cork free press and exeter and plymouth gazette of 2 july; and on 22 july the daily malta chronicle has him sending a telegram of respectful greeting to queen wilhelmina on the delegation's behalf. same initials, same district, thirteen years apart - from a prisoner's number to the head of the free state's farmers. no descent from the settler is claimed here. 

s: 2 Oct 1861, Burgersdorp – 8 Nov 1934, Standerton — buried WAKKERSTROOM · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe of burgersdorp 2 oct 1861, burgersdorp - 8 nov 1934, standerton - buried wakkerstroom · kolbe the second george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. his stone: "in liefvolle herinnering aan ons ouers - george augustus kolbe - geb. 2 oktober 1861 - oorl. 8 november 1934 - en susanna margaretha kolbe - geb. 26 oktober 1861 - oorl. 28 julie 1940 - hulle rus." born at burgersdorp, which is where the 1820 settler is buried and where the settler's twin son george augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. he is buried at wakkerstroom although he died at standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, two years apart in birth and twenty in death. and the birth date decides the prisoner: the 1902 pow record of wo 108/368 gives a george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom aged 40, and a man born 2 october 1861 was forty from october 1901 to october 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. the prisoner is this man. 17 september 2026 - and now he has parents. the last 214 images of the burgersdorp baptism register, film 008039088, hold his font: born 2 october 1861, baptised 12 january 1862 at burgersdorp, father g. a. kolbe, mother anna maria viljoen - familysearch 1:1:6fwf-yvjt, image 685. the stone gave a date and a town and this archive wrote that the descent was not documented; the register gives him a couple. he has two younger siblings in the same book. whether his father is the settler's twin son - the g.a. kolbe born 23 february 1836, who would have been twenty-five - is the next step and is not taken here. 16 september 2026 - the pow entry now has a folio: tna wo 108/368 folio 709, the war office list of boer prisoners of war numbers 1-32,561, which records him as a transvaaler, residence wakkerstroom, and held in natal. he is one of six kolbe men in that list, and the only one of the six not in the southern free state. 

s: 29 Jul 1863, baptised 11 Oct 1863 at Colesberg – 28 Sep 1954, Wakkerstroom — aged 91 · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom 29 jul 1863, baptised 11 oct 1863 at colesberg - 28 sep 1954, wakkerstroom - aged 91 · kolbe the settler's grandson, carrying his name entire, and the man the wakkerstroom kolbes descend from. baptised at colesberg in the year of his uncle frederick fortunatus barry's birth. married martha sophia klopper, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, maria johanna, was born at wakkerstroom in 1886. and his stone settles the identification beyond argument: "vader - george augustus - geb. 29 julie 1863 - oorl. 28 sept. 1954", which is the colesberg font date to the day. the 1902 pow record with residence wakkerstroom is not his: the other george augustus kolbe of that town was born 2 october 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. died at wakkerstroom on 28 september 1954, aged 91, which counts exactly from the colesberg font: born 29 july 1863, dead 28 september 1954. he outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

q: george mountjoy of kokstad c. 1862, orange free state - 12 may 1943, nyaninga, tongaat, natal - aged 81 · mountjoy the head of the other mountjoy family, the one this archive has twice said is not its own. his death notice, signed at bizana on 25 may 1943 by a son who was not present at the death, gives him as retired, of kokstad, east griqualand, born in the orange free state, a union national, eighty-one years old, married in community of property to mary mountjoy, born fischer, the marriage in the king williamstown district. he left movables, immovables, an estate over £300 and a will. nine children, named: minnie burger born mountjoy; maria kirsten born mountjoy; george mountjoy; christian mountjoy; emily lloyd born mountjoy; joseph mountjoy; alfred mountjoy; nellie bouwer born mountjoy; lettie van der sandt born mountjoy. they are named here and not made into people, because nothing yet joins this house to this archive's and a family chart is not a place to park a maybe. and question three fails again: father - "names unknown". mother - "names unknown: deceased". so the one line that could have connected or disconnected him from the cradock saddler's descendants is blank, exactly as it is blank on the saddler's own notice a century earlier. this archive's earlier judgement stands and is now better evidenced. the transkei mountjoys - lusikisiki, bizana, mnyameni, kokstad, flagstaff, traders and labour agents - were recorded as "not this family so far as anything shows". they are still that, but they are now a documented household rather than a scatter of index hits, and three of the ten estates this archive wanted belong to it.

gerthardus lodewikus booysen - - - · booyzen the one document that names him has been weakened, and by somebody who had not seen it. on 14 september 2026 pieter van zyl, answering this archive's g2g question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household - and added, from memory, that he thought a child of petrus jacobus was called gerhardus lodewicus. he is right, and the child is on the same sheet: line 12 of that very notice names jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen among the eight children. so the name this archive takes from line 3, for the dead man's father, is the back half of his son's name, eight lines below, in one clerk's hand - and the half that is dropped, jan, is the name de villiers gives as the real father. this does not prove the father was jan and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. it removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. the top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. he still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him. 15 september 2026 - and the last escape route is closed. this archive's standing objection was that de villiers's 1893 original was revised by pama in 1981, and a revision can move a man; if the 1981 edition had relocated petrus jacobus, the death notice would stand. riel smit, who has the 1981 edition: "yes, de villiers & pama (1981) still place petrus jacobus (b3c4d7) b. 21 sept 1788 under jan b3c4." pieter van zyl adds that he searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and a magdalena de beer and could not find one. four things now point one way and the only thing pointing the other is line 3 of notice 678. the spine is still not being moved on this: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. what ends it is the baptism entry of 21 september 1788 - the register de villiers compiled his entry from, naming the father in a contemporary hand. it is now the first item on the errands page.

james montjoy c. 1782, "europe" - sep 1827, cradock · mountjoy saddler. owned a house and erf at cradock worth £90. his 1840 death notice gives his parents as not known - the oldest document here, and the top of this line. 15 september 2026 - a man who slept in his house says where he came from. john montgomery, founder of burgersdorp, in the friend of the free state of 25 november 1869, recalling his arrival at cradock in january 1822 when the place held about six people: "messrs. solomon and s.m. de beer, the rev. mr. evans, mr. p. gie, james mountjoy (a saddler, who was discharged from the 21st light dragoons), the two messrs. ziervogel, mr. heilberg, fieldcornet b.j. vorster, and gert van deventer. after some trouble i obtained lodgings for the night from mr. mountjoy." there is no room in a village of six for two saddlers of one name. the 21st light dragoons were the cavalry of the cape garrison from the 1806 expedition until the end of that decade, so he arrived in uniform - which is exactly why no cape document can say where he was from, and why the marriage register of 1817 rules a line through the column and leaves it empty. he was not a passenger on anything. the record that answers it is wo 97 at kew, the chelsea discharge papers, arranged by regiment before 1855, which give a soldier's parish and county of birth, his age at enlistment and his trade. 16 september 2026 - his discharge now has a deadline, and it came from the london papers. the 21st light dragoons were relieved at york in may 1806 and sailed from portsmouth for the cape; part of them went on to south america in 1806 and came back to the cape in 1807; parliament complained in march 1809 that they had been sent "where they could have nothing to do"; a large reinforcement followed in october 1810; sir john cradock reviewed them and pronounced them "in the highest state of discipline"; a draft of 140 men embarked for the cape in october 1813; and then, in a letter from the cape dated 1 and 10 september 1817 and printed in five london papers that november, "the 21st light dragoons have embarked for india". he married at graaff-reinet on 9 march 1817. his regiment sailed for india six months later. a man who married in march 1817 and was keeping a house and a saddler's trade at cradock by january 1822 was discharged at the cape before september 1817, and what he was choosing between was a wife at graaff-reinet and a transport to madras. the town he settled in is named after the governor who reviewed his regiment.

jan hendrik kolbe 5 jul 1849, baptised fauresmith 9 oct 1849 - 1924 · kolbe his parents are named in a baptism register, and the question this archive asked all month is answered. *south africa, free state dutch reformed church records, 1848-1956*: **born 5 july 1849, baptised at fauresmith on 9 october 1849**, son of **jan gerson eliese kolbe and anna jacoba van der merwe**. the same entry is indexed a second time in the cape town archives collection, as "hendrik kolbe", with the identical two dates and the same two parents - one event, two indexings, which is agreement between transcribers and not between witnesses. **so he is the commandant's son from a document**, where this archive had him from a user tree since 20 september and would not adopt it. **and it explains the farm.** he farmed the commandant's farm, and until this morning that was the nearest thing to an answer. he married rose maria mccabe at bloemfontein on 4 june 1872 - *south africa, civil marriage records*, familysearch 1:1:6zhb-xq1r - and the register image was read on 27 september 2026. it enters him as **23**, **jongelieden**, **veeboer**, living at **leeuwberg (blfn.)**; his bride's residence is written **"dito"**, the same farm. leeuwberg is where commandant j.g.e. kolbe died in 1868, and where the register had placed the commandant's widow eleven months earlier, at her own second marriage. a twenty-three-year-old kolbe running stock on that farm in 1872 is exactly what a son of that house would be doing, and his year of birth sits correctly among the children of a man who married in 1843. it is still not proof. a farm is not a father; brothers, nephews and hired kin all live on farms, and this archive has already been caught once this month reading a household as a parentage. the form cannot settle it and never could - it has no parents' columns, which is a correction against this archive's own assumption rather than a disappointment. he signed himself *j. h. kolbe*. the second witness signed **g. a. kolbe** - a name this family carries in three generations, and one more reason to want vab mhg m777, which would name all twelve children at once. he is the second of two kolbes to marry a mccabe in ten months. **and on 2 august 1869 he and his brother took church membership at bloemfontein on the same day** - "john henry kolbe" and "willem johannes kolbe", both entered that date in the free state registers, which was willem johannes's twenty-second birthday and fifteen months after their father died. **john henry is jan hendrik anglicised**, and under that spelling the registers give him five children by rose maria mccabe: **john gerson eliezer** - the commandant's name entire - elizabeth magdalena, ada francis, anna jacoba and rosa euphemia. a man names his eldest son after his own father, and this one did.

s: 1844 or 1845 — three sources give three years – 11 Mar 1906, Smithfield, Orange River Colony · Kolbe
q: johan casimir kolbe 1844 or 1845 - three sources give three years - 11 mar 1906, smithfield, orange river colony · kolbe named in both his parents' death notices and in this archive's people list until 21 september 2026 in neither. the settler's death notice, signed m. kolbe - margaret, the widow - at colesberg in january 1845, names ten children and he is the fifth of them. margaret downing's own notice of 25 november 1867, signed by her son-in-law g. d. o. werdmuller, names him again, and it is careful about the dead: mary elizabeth is entered as "(dead), who was married to george f. enslin" and he is not. so he was alive at about twenty-three, twenty-three years after his father died. the forename is the point. this archive already called the family's forenames extraordinary - hachilah machilah, gerson eliezar, fortunatus - and listed casimir among them. a compiled register report published on a barry family website in 2012 gives him as johan casmier, ninth of thirteen, and that spelling was treated here as a name the archive had never held. it is a third spelling of a name in two primary documents - the family list already carried the variant "casiner". and the name outlived him in south africa. this archive's own register carries three men of it out of south africa, civil marriage records, 1801-1974: johan hendrik casimir kolbe, born 1863, who married gertruida jacomina louw; johan casimir kolbe, who married elizabeth geertruida pienaar; and johan casimir kolbe, born 1934, who married maria monica van der walt. a shared surname is not a relationship and none of the three is joined to this house - they are index rows, and they are here because a rare forename recurring in the same country for ninety years is a thing to follow, not a thing to assume. **that sentence is kept because it was wrong by six days.** it read: *nothing is known of his own life: no baptism, no marriage, no death. the bethulie and colesberg registers are where to look.* **colesberg was the right answer and the baptism was the wrong question.** **27 september 2026 - he has a life, and none of it is a font.** searched not on his own name but on his **mother's**: **margaret downing**. **his death names both his parents outright** - *south africa, orange free state, civil death registration*, familysearch 1:1:d9sm-k2n2: **johan casimis kolbe, died 11 march 1906 at smithfield, o.r.c., aged 60**, born in the **cape colony**, **son of george augustus kolbe and margaret downing**. until today he existed here only inside his parents' death notices; now a civil register puts him in the household from the other end of his life. **and colesberg has him twice, in the register this archive was looking in.** he took **church membership at colesberg on 31 march 1866**, and his **marriage banns were called at colesberg on 1 may 1867** - to **elizabeth geertruida pienaar**. their daughter **adriana** is in the cape register, and the free state registers give five more: **elizabeth augusta, anna sophia, johanna, george augustus and margaret dewning** - **he named a son for his father and a daughter for his mother**, which is this family's habit and is the best corroboration a namesake can give. **his estate exists**: *orange free state probate records from the master of the supreme court*, probate **1906 at smithfield**, not ordered and not read. **three sources, three birth years, and a document already held here settles two of them.** the family list says **1844 at bethulie**; the death registration's age of 60 implies **1846**; the probate index says **1845**. **he is the fifth of the ten children named on his father's death notice, signed at colesberg in january 1845** - so **1846 is impossible**, and an age at death is the weakest of the three. **1844 or 1845, and the font would say which.** the baptism is not in the cape dutch reformed index: fifteen records answer *casimir* in that whole collection and not one is a baptism of his. 

johan christiaan pietersen bapt. 28 apr 1810 - - · mountjoy a person nobody had. the second of anna catharina slier's two sons by hermanus pietersen, baptised 28 april 1810 - thirteen months after his brother - and therefore a second half-brother to the montjoy children. he appears on nothing else in this archive, and he is here because de villiers's volume 3 lists him on the line below one this archive had already read wrong. 

johan gottlieb kolbe c. 1764 - 18 nov 1845, london · kolbe he had eight sons, and this archive knew of one. his son's obituary in the grahamstown journal of 19 december 1844 calls george augustus "the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq. of brunswick-square, london". seven brothers, all dead before december 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive - and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 conduit street household holds three women and no sons. the obituary also puts him at brunswick square, in bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at conduit street in mayfair, a mile and a half away. both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once - off the family tree's lamb's conduit street - so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. "esq.", not "tailor". and he is in the london gazette, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 september 1836, dissolving the copartnership of "john gottlob kolbe and david fletcher, of conduit-street, bond-street, in the county of middlesex, tailors". that is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source - and it pushes him back to conduit street in 1836. and the death is now a gro reference: freebmd gives one kolbe death in all of england and wales for 1845-46 - "deaths dec 1845, kolbe, john gottlob, st geo han sq, vol 1, page 35". the district matches the census; the name form john gottlob matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. found in the 1841 census, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. he is at conduit street, st george hanover square, sub-district may fair, aged 76 - four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's lamb's conduit street. and his birth county is entered as "foreign", which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not english. ho107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, schedule 38. three women share that schedule: marianne, 35, charlotte, 30, and amelia a., 25. tailor. died at 34 conduit street, mayfair - not lamb's conduit street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. 16 september 2026 - the address argument is over, and he had two wives. the westminster rate books index him one hundred and twenty-one times between 1800 and 1831, under twenty-four spellings of his forename - gothel, gotleb, gotleib, gotlieb, gotliel, gotlob, gotlobe, goltief, gottieb, gottiel, gottlieb, gottlob, gutlieb, kottieb, gilliet and once "jos gottiel". in 1800 he is at broad street north, st james piccadilly, folio 41 - which independently corroborates the printed 1799 list of 234 master tailors, "kolbe, john, 18 broad-street, soho". from 1811 to 1831 he is at church street south, st anne's soho, year after year, and the 1829 land tax return says the same. brunswick square appears in no rate book, no land tax return, no census and no burial register - those are westminster sources and bloomsbury would not be in them, so they cannot disprove it, but soho 1800-1831, st george hanover square in 1841 and a death there in 1845 leaves no window for it. and the burial is now a register entry rather than a tree claim: westminster burials, city of westminster archives centre - died 18 november 1845, buried 26 november 1845 at st john the baptist, great marlborough street, page 7, year of birth given as 1764. the date matches the tree's "26 november 1845, entry 55, grave 7" to the day and the "7" matches; the church does not. 20 september 2026 - he writes, and he signs himself. msb 751 at the national library of south africa is a letter of four sides headed "london august 23. 1830", opening "dear george" and signed "your affectionate father, j g kolbe". it is the first document in this archive he wrote himself - everything else is somebody writing about him. it does not carry a street address: the heading is "london" and nothing finer, so it does not settle brunswick square against conduit street, which is what this archive most hoped for. what it does carry: his son's acceptance by the london missionary society in the father's own words, dr philip carrying an earlier letter to the cape, mr miles of the society calling at the house, henry dying of dropsy and "resigned to the catastrophe", milne and elizabeth - "betsey" - removed to edinburgh, charlotte sending an evangelical magazine, a suit of black clothes sent out for a newly accepted missionary, the death of george iv and the french revolution of july 1830 as fresh news, and a request that his son fact-check a baboon story in a magazine. and the line that counts most: "kind love from your sisters & brother" - sisters plural, brother singular. of the eight sons, two were alive in august 1830. 20 september, read again from the file instead of from a mail preview, and it carries more. dr philip is not just the courier - "dr philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the l.m.s. as you may well imagine, he has promised to write to you a letter by the first opportunity". he sends a box: a suit of black clothes for george, and a jacket and waistcoat for john with a further jacket, "tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". a year of newspapers, one number lost by henry. and the house has friends with names, the first in this archive who simply knew them: mr & mrs stanhope, mr and mrs warner, and mrs field and her daughters - "the eldest, miss mary, that was, has married a mr bellew, a surgeon". two of his four pages go on a story from the mirror about a scottish colonist near the xhosa whose wife was carried off by orang-outangs and recovered after two years as their queen - and he does not believe a word of it: "here we look upon the story as a fictious & romance… i should be glad to hear from you, whether that report may be founded in truth, or falsehood." a tailor of seventy, reading a cheap weekly, writing to the one man he knew who was actually there to ask whether it was true. 21 september 2026 - and the story is found, and he was right. it is "a singular letter from southern africa, communicated by mr. hogg, the ettrick shepherd", the mirror of literature, amusement, and instruction, volume xiv (1829), pages 313-318 - fiction by james hogg, author of the private memoirs and confessions of a justified sinner, printed as though it were a settler's letter home. every detail he recalled is in it: the chief karoo offering oxen and "a choice virgin to boot" for the settler's wife, "he foretold i should repent it", captain johnstone, the wife "carried across the river by a band of pongos, (ourang-outangs)", and her discovery as their queen. and the detail he got wrong is why five searches for it failed: he thought the colonist was called "either williams, or williamson", and the narrator is anonymous - it is his son who is called william. his first wife mary died 2 august 1814 aged 46 and his second, also mary, died 15 august 1824 aged 36, both buried in the german lutheran church register, tna rg 4/4631 - which is why one mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. and the london gazette holds five notices, not the one this archive had. 12 may 1824 - the partnership of john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, tailors, dissolved. 30 september 1836 - kolbe and david fletcher of conduit-street dissolved. 21 march 1845 - "john gotlieb kolbe and richard davies, of conduit-street, bond-street, tailors, has been dissolved by mutual consent", eight months before he died and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary's "esq. of brunswick-square" has to be set against. 1824 was the year it all went: the partnership dissolved in may, his second wife dead in august, and his son in the insolvent debtors' lists in october and november. 16 september, later - and the 1799 tailors' list has a twin. in april and may 1834 the london press printed the roll of "considerably more than three hundred of the master tailors of the metropolis" who met at willis's rooms, st james's-street, to resist the grand national consolidated trades' union, and the entry reads "kolbe and fletcher, conduit-street" - morning post 30 april, globe 30 april and 10 may, old england 4 may, morning herald 10 may, london courier 10 may, true sun 10 may, public ledger 12 may. seven newspapers, one line. 20 september 2026 - and a historian called him an apothecary. the dsab draft entry on his son opens "die seun van j.g.kolbe, 'n duitse apteker wat in londen woonagtig was". the german is right and the london is right and the trade is his son's - george augustus sailed in 1820 as an apothecary, and the apothecary has been handed back up to the father. it is the only thing in that entry this archive can show to be wrong, and it can only show it because it read the rate books. it closes the gap: the rate books had him in soho to 1831 and the gazette at conduit street by 1836; he was at conduit street, with fletcher, by 29 april 1834. and it rhymes with the first list thirty-five years earlier - in december 1799 one of 234 masters over the combination acts, a young man at 18 broad-street; in april 1834 a firm with a partner and a bond street address, seventy years old, on the masters' side of the same argument. 

s: 1863, Orange Free State – 14 Sep 1923, Bloemfontein — aged 60 · Kolbe
q: johan hendrik cassimir kolbe 1863, orange free state - 14 sep 1923, bloemfontein - aged 60 · kolbe the eleventh of the twelve, and he never married. his civil death registration completes field 14 as **john gerson eliezer kolbe, farmer** and field 15 as **anna jacoba van der merwe** - the commandant and his wife, both named in full, the mother's maiden surname given correctly. a stock farmer of georgia, district bloemfontein, entered as dutch, born in the orange free state, buried at georgia; the medical practitioner dr s. a. de kock; the informant signed from thaba'nchu in the capacity of arranging the burial. dead at sixty on 14 september 1923 after a last illness the form records in two columns at once - **two days**, and **many years**. he is entered as unmarried and the form then gives an age at marriage of 24. both are on the page; field 6 says unmarried and field 7, which only applies if he was married, carries a number. this archive is not going to choose between them and does not need to - nothing here turns on it. two forms, one mother, two answers. his sister catharina wilhelmina's registration of 1909 was asked for the same mother's maiden surname and was given her married one, kolbe, after a crossed-out word. his gives van der merwe. **the field is identical; the informants were not**, and that is the whole difference between a document that closes a question and one that merely repeats a household.
