q: john barry - - 1796 was the other man's year - 1853, de bruins poort · barry one profile holding two men - and on 14 september 2026 they came apart. the yorkshire man is now a life: born at whitby in 1796; resident at bilsdale midcable when he took a licence on 2 october 1838 to marry margaret jackson of beadlam at helmsley; and in the 1851 census a ship owner at ship yards, ruswarp, whitby, aged 55, married, head of his household - the only john barry of that age in the whole yorkshire census. john barry deaths are then registered in the whitby district in 1858 and in 1860. he outlived the cape man, who died at de bruins poort in 1853, by at least five years. they are two men. what this archive still does not have is the cape one: no birth, no arrival, no burial. and a caution worth keeping - a whitby ship owner is exactly the kind of man whose son could be born at sea, which is what john augustus barry's death notice says of 1819. that coincidence is not evidence, and the censuses say it is not the same man.

s: 7 Jul 1822, Uitenhage – 3 Apr 1868, the farm Leeuwberg — aged 45 · Kolbe
q: john gerson eliezar kolbe 7 jul 1822, uitenhage - 3 apr 1868, the farm leeuwberg - aged 45 · kolbe a stock farmer, and it is his daughter who says so: her 1909 death registration completes field 14 - father's name in full, and occupation - as "jan gersem eliezer kolbe, stock farmer", which is the first trade this archive has for him from a document rather than from an obituary's account of his soldiering. the settler's eldest child, and until today a line in a table. his obituary - grahamstown journal, 15 april 1868, headed "death of commandant kolbe" - gives the whole man. born 7 july 1822; married 3 april 1843 to anna jacoba van der merwe; died 3 april 1868, on his wedding anniversary, at the farm leeuwberg, of typhus or typhoid caught on commando - "thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war". he had settled on kaalspruit about 1850 and lies there - and he confirms the farm himself. a lost-property advertisement he placed in the friend on 9 march 1864 is signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit" (the address as the paper printed it). the friend's own obituary transcription reads "[randspruit]", bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man's own address settles it. that advertisement also puts the two brothers in one document: it concerns "a promissory note, date 9th march 1864, drawn by george augustus kolbe in favor of j.g.e. kolbe, payable 4 months after date for £154 stg" - lost on the market square at bloemfontein. he left a widow and twelve children - "of the eight sons and four daughters he has left behind him", which is the friend of the free state's own wording and a count the grahamstown reprint drops. only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; two sons had been serving with him in the field and "proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers". none of the twelve is named and none is in this archive. 20 september 2026 - a collaborative tree names them, and it is not this family's own. a geni profile for frederik fortunatus kolbe, born 22 october 1857 at bloemfontein and dead there 18 december 1930, gives him as son of commandant.gen. john gherson eliezer kolbe and anna jacoba, and lists as his siblings catharina wilhelmina magdalena pienaar anderson, george augustus, general willem johannes, jan hendrik and petrus jacobus "and 6 others" - which is twelve. this is from a user tree, not from a document, and none of the twelve is adopted here on it - it is a lead and not a witness. but two of its claims match documents this archive reached independently: his wife maria petronella elizabeth antoinette and daughter rosa magdalene against the 1890 bloemfontein baptism already held, and his daughter maria margaretha downing rousseau against tab mhg 5450/68, an orphan index entry here that now has a father. vab mhg m777 is still the document that would prove them, and it is a better thing to order now that there is something to check it against. he was commandant of the district, a justice of the peace, a director of the bloemfontein bank and a deacon of the dutch reformed church, and he had spoken in the volksraad in may 1867. he had refused public life for twelve years after the abandonment, having protested the british withdrawal and applied to sir george clerk for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, "he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the free state". and on his deathbed, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present that this state had taken too much land from the basutos, that he had always thought so and had said so in the raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the governor for an equitable boundary. 20 september 2026 - a historian's draft names him too, and names the war. the dsab entry on his father says the eldest son "j.g.e. kolbe (1822-68), was later op leeuberg naby bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die tweede sotho-vrystaatoorlog roem verwerf as kommandant". both years match this archive to the year - born 7 july 1822, dead 3 april 1868 - and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. it is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. and it names what killed him: the obituary said only "our miserable war"; the war was the second sotho-free state war. and he may be in the 1830 letter, aged eight. read from the file rather than from a mail preview, msb 751 encloses "a jacket & waistcoat for john & a further jacket also for him, tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". clothes for a growing child, sent from soho to the cape in august 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. if it is him it is the earliest document in this archive that mentions him. "his old father" is the difficulty and is not glossed over - the writer is his grandfather, and this is an inference, not a reading. **11 october 2026 - a published history of the free state mourns him by name, and it has been sitting in the open since 1876.** h. j. hofstede, *geschiedenis van den oranje-vrijstaat* (1876), is out of copyright and its full text is free on the internet archive. **it names him seventeen times.** in an aside the author cannot help making, he writes of **"den kommandant van bloemfontein j. g. e. kolbe"**, taken from them **"door een noodlottige koorts"** - by a fatal fever - **"niet op 't bed van eer, maar in het midden zijner betrekkingen"**: not on the bed of honour, but in the midst of his relations, **"bemind en geacht door alle rechtgeaarde vrijstaters als een goed en verstandig medeburger en een voorganger in den strijd tegen geweldenarij en roof"**. **that is a stranger's verdict on him, in print, eight years after he died**, and it is the first this archive has had from anybody who was not a newspaper or a relative. **it also names his command**: he is the commandant of bloemfontein, which this archive had nowhere - it had the farm, the district and the rank, never the seat. **and it agrees with the obituary about what killed him without having read it.** the grahamstown journal said typhus or typhoid caught on commando; hofstede says a fatal fever and is careful to say he did not die in action but at home among his people - **which is exactly what a man who carries a camp disease back to his own farm looks like**, and the two accounts are the same event told by two men who wanted different things from it. **on the date they differ by one day and the archive's stands.** hofstede gives **4 april 1868**. the obituary gives **3 april**, and 3 april 1868 was a **friday**, and it was his **twenty-fifth wedding anniversary** - three facts that lock together and that a historian writing in 1876 had no reason to hold. **4 april is recorded as a variant and is not adopted.** **and it is the first account of what he actually did on commando.** he and commandant roos were sent by the president as **gijzelaars - hostages for moshesh's personal safety** - so that moshesh would come in to the meeting; the chief came with his principal sons an hour later. at **klokkelani** he surrounded the basotho and sent word to the hoofdkommandant, who came up with the armstrong gun. at **the thiemie** he went up a footpath with commandant prinsloo and two hundred men, reached the summit with fifty, and then **held the captured position that divided the mountain in two** while the others cleared the northern point; the day's taking was **10,657 cattle, 5,468 sheep and goats and 1,007 horses**, and he came back into camp at sunset soaked through and spent. **this is the man the obituary called a leader, doing it.** **one kolbe in the book is not established as him**: a kolbe climbs a krans on other men's shoulders with hunton, owen, raaff and the hangers in a different action under commandant wessels, and nothing in the passage says which kolbe he is. **that action has now been placed, by reading the pages before it.** they are the **assaults on thaba bosiu in august 1865** - the ones louw wepener died in - and the page that runs into it ends with the stormers reaching **"de eerste loodrecht opgaande rots, die omtrent 20 voet hoog was"**, the first sheer rock about twenty feet high. **seven men got up it on each other's shoulders and one of them was a kolbe.** **he is still not established as this man**, who was a commandant and would not be named bare among a captain and five burghers; a son is as likely, and two of his sons were serving with him. **and there is a second name in the same book that is harder to put down.** on **6 april 1866**, three men were allowed by sephanja to go up and bring away **louw wepener's bones**: jan jonathan durand, franz holm, and **"jan colbe"**. **the archive's own man is "jan gersem eliezer kolbe"** - that is his daughter's wording on her 1909 death registration - **so the given name is exactly right, and that is precisely why it is not adopted.** **the printed page has now been read, and it says colbe.** the leaf was found by parsing the scan's own `_djvu.xml`, whose page objects carry the ocr leaf by leaf; the colbe falls on **leaf 211, printed folio 160**, and the type on that page is unambiguous: **"durand, franz holm en jan colbe door sefoni (sephanja) toegelaten om de beenderen van l. wepener weg te nemen."** **the ocr was faithful and the spelling is the book's own**, in a volume that sets *kolbe* seventeen times for the commandant. **so the resemblance is weaker than it looked and this archive takes nothing from it.** the page is kept for a different reason: it says the bones were buried by j. j. durand at wepener's last dwelling place, **constantia in the district of bethulie** - the district the settler helped open as the bushman school - and it dates the failed storming to **15 august 1865**, naming the *timie* as the mountain taken later. **that later mountain is the thiemie, and the man who held its summit was this commandant.** **and a second book has what no other source has: a document he wrote.** d. c. f. moodie, *history of the battles and adventures of the british, the boers and the zulus in southern africa* (1888), **page 93**, read as an image and not only as text: **"a report from commandant j. g. e. kolbe to commandant botha, dated platberg, 2nd nov., 1867, gives an account of the capture of some caverns and strongholds at mariendall."** moodie summarises it rather than printing it: one boer killed and two severely wounded; **eleven of the enemy killed as far as was known; 120 women and children taken out of the caverns and put across the caledon; twenty wagon loads of corn taken.** the next report on the same page is **commandant j. c. botha** to the president, platberg, 7 november 1867 - **which gives botha his initials** - and botha is the commandant who stood beside him on the thiemie in hofstede. **two books twelve years apart, neither citing the other, put the same two men together.** **what surrounds it on the page is moodie's doing and is not hidden here.** immediately above, moodie quotes the rev. mr jousse writing from thaba bosigo in october 1867 that in a raid nearby people were **"killed as dogs indistinctly men, women, and children"**, the women and children outnumbering the men. **kolbe's report, as summarised, does not describe killing women and children** - it says they were taken out and put across the river - **and the juxtaposition is the historian's, not the record's.** both are set down, because an archive that prints a man's commendations and not the war they were earned in is not describing the same war. **the report itself is now a thing to look for**, with a date, a place and an addressee to look for it by. 

john gottlob kolbe - - - · kolbe a tailor of conduit street, mayfair, and the grade rests on paper rather than on the tree. four independent documents call him john gottlob where the family tree calls him johan gottlieb, and this archive follows the documents: his will of 1842, a prerogative court of canterbury register copy; his death in 1845; the marriage at st leonard's, shoreditch on 20 january 1819 where his son swore a false age; and his own letter of 23 august 1830 to that son at the cape. this note said only "of the london kolbes" until 11 october 2026, under a heading that promises what the archive holds. 

s: bapt. 29 Jul 1800, St James, Westminster – 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church · Kolbe
q: john henry kolbe bapt. 29 jul 1800, st james, westminster - 13 apr 1832, buried 22 apr 1832, german lutheran church · kolbe one of the eight sons, and the one who lived longest of those found. baptised 29 july 1800, father john, mother mary, batch i02559-1. tna rg 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 april 1832, buried 22 april, aged 32 - twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. and he speaks. old bailey, session of 13 january 1819, trial t18190113-149 - richard kerr indicted for stealing "one coat, value 6l., the property of john henry kolbe". his own deposition: "my father is a tailor, and lives in church-street, soho. on the 9th of january, about eleven o'clock at night, i stopped at the star and crown public-house, westminster, and left my coat over my horse's head - i had a chaise standing at the door; i saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him - i went out, and missed my coat." not guilty. he was eighteen, and his brother george augustus sailed for algoa bay the following year. it is the only voice this archive has from the soho house, and it corroborates the rate books' address from a source that had no interest in it. and the london gazette says what became of him. 12 may 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of "john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, in the county of middlesex, tailors" dissolved - father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. then 9 october and 16 november 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the insolvent debtors lists, petitions to be heard at portugal-street, lincoln's-inn fields on 5 november: "kolbe, john henry (sued as henry kolbe), formerly of no. 22, norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, and late of no. 4, mansfield-place". he was twenty-four, out of the family business and out of soho in the same year his stepmother died, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 september 2026 - and his father writes about his dying. msb 751, the letter of 23 august 1830 to his brother at the cape: "henry had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down the dropsy, of which he bears still the symptoms… i trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his god… he appears at present to be resigned to the catastrophe." he had twenty months left. and the same letter's closing - "kind love from your sisters & brother" - makes him the last of the eight sons alive besides george augustus, so that the obituary's "last remaining of eight sons" became true on 13 april 1832, twelve years before it was printed. and he married three months after the trial: westminster marriages - john henry kolbe and matilda ford, 26 april 1819, st margaret westminster, both of that parish. he was eighteen. a mary ann maria ford kolbe married at whitechapel in the first quarter of 1847 - gro index volume az, 840, page 16 - and "ford" carried as a forename is how families carried a mother's maiden name. she is very probably his daughter. and the press gives his trade, which the gazette did not. law chronicle, commercial and bankruptcy register, 13 january 1825: "kolbe john henry, of norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, last of mansfield-st., kentish town, tailor, draper" - so he set up on his own account in his father's trade, and the gazette's "mansfield-place" is mansfield street, kentish town. the may 1824 dissolution was reported in at least six london papers, all of them putting his name first: "j. h. kolbe and j. g. kolbe, church-street, soho, tailors". and the 1830 letter shows him doing an ordinary thing. packing a year of newspapers for the cape, his father notes one number missing - "the one of the 4th of decr last, which cannot be found, supposing that henry, who has them every week, after i have done with them, - has lost". the father read the paper first and the son had it after. it is the only description this archive has of what anybody in that house did with an ordinary evening, and he had four months to live when it was written.

what was wrong was only the date this archive kept for her. it is the same fault the johan casimir row diagnosed in september, in the same file: a search of the index is not a search of the holdings. the answer was also on a photograph this archive has had all along. the burgersdorp monument is on the kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as "also his relict margaret downing…" and stopped there. the stone goes on: "born in london 23 february 1803 and died at burghersdorp 2_ november 1867." her birth is now a date - 23 february 1803, where this archive had "c. 1804" - and the death is settled at 1867. her son's obituary of 15 april 1868 said she had died "about three months since", which would have been january 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. the day is a 2 and a digit that will not resolve at any magnification, and is not guessed. the cape estate ran on: mooc 13/1/253 no. 2, "downing, margaret, widow of kolbe, george augustus. liquidation and distribution account", 1869 - and she had made a will of her own in 1854, mooc 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. married at fifteen in shoreditch, signing with a mark. died owning a house and a farm. 20 september 2026 - her mother is still nobody, and that is now a tested position rather than a gap. a user tree gave her as mary king pooley (1768-1834); s: 1840, Colesberg — from the family list only – — · Kolbe
q: peter benjamin kolbe 1840, colesberg - from the family list only - - · kolbe **27 september 2026 - still in no document, and now that is a tested statement rather than an absence of trying.** the cape dutch reformed registers were searched for **peter**, **benjamin** and **rector** together: **five records in the entire collection**, and every one of them somebody else - two petrus jacobuses, a pieter joubert kolbe, and the two fatherless entries this family already has. **no colesberg baptism for 1840.** **the nil is controlled but it is not strong**, and the reason is visible in the same result set: this collection indexes his own brother's 1838 baptism with the father as the bare word **"kolbe"** and no forename, and his eldest sister's the same way. **an index that loses the father's name can lose a child's**, so this is evidence that he is not in the index and weaker evidence that he was never at the font. the man who may explain the rector, and who is in no document. this archive has carried him as "keetor peter benjamin", born 1840 at colesberg, from the family list. keetor is not a name. the 2012 barry report gives the same person as peter rector kolbe, and rector is - so on the ordinary reading, "keetor" is "rector" misread out of a hand, and the compiled report is the better witness to the form of the name even though it is the weaker source overall. that matters because of a child born forty-two years later. this archive holds anton rector kolbe barry, born 3 november 1882 and baptised at burgersdorp in 1883, and has never been able to say where his rector came from. a great-uncle of the name would say it, and namesake reasoning is how the fortunatus name was traced across three families. but the same report splits him in two, listing peter rector and benjamin as separate children where the family list has one man carrying all three forenames - so the report inflates its own count, and this is one of the places it does it. and the documents do not help him. the settler's 1845 notice names ten children and he is not among them; margaret downing's 1867 notice names the survivors and he is not there either. a boy born in 1840 would have been four when his father died and a minor children's name is exactly what a death notice records. so he died before 1845, or he does not belong to this family, and the archive has not been able to tell which since it first raised it. nothing here is adopted: two compiled sources agreeing about a forename are still two compiled sources. a colesberg baptism for 1840 would settle him, and it has not been read.

s: c. Oct 1874, Cape Province – 14 May 1940, East Lynne, Pretoria · Booyzen
q: stephanus francois booyzen c. oct 1874, cape province - 14 may 1940, east lynne, pretoria · booyzen the stone is now read, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. silverton, pretoria, a double stone under one base reading booyzen: "'n simbool van liefde - aan my dierbare eggenoot en ons vader - stefanus francois - ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 - sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'heer, dit is gods wil. ges. 75:1". his birth is now exact: 29 september 1874, where this archive had only "c. october 1874". and a pillar between the two halves lists twelve children by their household names - ouboet · ousie · bessie · betie · henna · evert · ✝baba · fanie · willie · pietie · johan · hennie - one of them marked dead with a cross. this archive had almost none of them. they are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. his grave is found and photographed: "booyzen stefanus francois 1874-1940", silverton main cemetery, pretoria - a joint stone with his wife, "booyzen beatrix magdalena catharina nee boshoff 1889-1977". both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. he died at east lynne, pretoria, and lies at silverton. image located, not yet read. prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 28 against this archive's c. october 1874, which would have made him 26. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. and then the prisoner number led somewhere else entirely. the medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a stephanus francois booysen, burger, whose pow number is 18463 - the same number as the register - and it says he was a zarp, one of the zar's police, based at pretoria. quoting a city coins auction catalogue of november 2020 that described his abo medal and the papers with it: in action at talana, modder spruit, colenso, platrand (wagon hill) where he was wounded in the right leg above the knee, spion kop and dalmanutha - the zarps' famous last stand. his applications were completed by his commanding officer, commandant j. p. de la c. schroeder. he was one of forty-two boers taken at tolosberg in the waterval valley on 25 april 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to india. this archive has not seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. what it does to the dispute: he is numbered 18463 and david schalk booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at east lynne, pretoria, which is the district all three were taken in. that is a fourth point favouring david schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. it is still not a document naming a parent. parentage disputed - see below. a son of the second marriage, and a messelaar - a mason, like his half-brother willem hermanus at indwe. his 1940 sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only "oorlede" for both parents. married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff at mosselbaai on 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 - he 30 and a jonkman, she sixteen with her parents consenting. eleven children; left immovable property and a will. the register gives his residence as pretoria, and eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria - whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called stephanus francois - remarried in that same city. this archive placed him under petrus jacobus on his birth year alone. it is marked serious on the disputed page and it is not decided.

s: 1878, Dordrecht – 14 Jun 1898, her husband’s residence, Barkly East — aged 20 · Mountjoy
q: wilhelmina ernestina mountjoy 1878, dordrecht - 14 jun 1898, her husband's residence, barkly east - aged 20 · mountjoy a mountjoy daughter who died forty years too early to be counted. her death notice, filed at barkly east on 19 august 1898 and numbered 2345, is read: born at dordrecht, dead at twenty at her husband's residence, a farmer's wife, married to andries johan brummer - his third forename is written and this archive cannot read it - and leaving one minor son. and line three names her parents: father john james mountjoy, mother maria louisa bertha, the surname trailing into a single capital and a flourish that is not legible. that is almost the barkly east household and it is not adopted as it. the man this archive holds is james jonathan mountjoy, retired builder, recorded here under the variants james john and jakobus jonathan, who married maria louisa bertha kumm at dordrecht in community of property - a surname with five spellings across seven baptisms, so an illegible one is what you would expect. three forenames match exactly, the town of birth is the town of the marriage, and the town of death is theirs. one document says no, and it is the better document. the distribution account of that man's estate, kab mooc 6/9/5047: 58379, pays eleven heirs in 1938 - nine living children, and gwendoline and aubrey diesel taking half a tenth each as the children of a daughter who had died in 1923. if this woman were an eleventh child, her own son would have had the same claim by representation, and there is no brummer in that account. the innocent explanation is that the boy died before 1938 without issue, which for a child born by 1898 is ordinary. the other explanation is that the father on this notice is a different john james mountjoy. a second arithmetic to watch: maria louisa bertha kumm's age at death puts her birth at about october 1860, which would make her seventeen when this daughter was born. possible, and tight. what would settle it: the dordrecht baptism register for 1878, or her own marriage record. until one of them is read she is a person here and not a daughter of that house.

s: baptised Graaff-Reinet 29 Sep 1861 — no birth date is recorded – — · Barry
q: william frederick thomas barry baptised graaff-reinet 29 sep 1861 - no birth date is recorded - - · barry the other missing barry child, and he is invisible for the opposite reason to his sister. she has no surname in the index; he has the same name as his brother. william fredrik barry was born 23 august 1853 and baptised at burgersdorp; this william frederick thomas was born 29 september 1861 and baptised at graaff-reinet, eight years later, to the same parents - "margaret wilhelmina kolbe + john barry". a search for william barry returns the 1853 child and stops, and nothing in the result says there is a second. by this family's own practice the first william must have died - a baptism is not done twice, which is exactly what this archive concluded about the two catherine mary sophias. the "william who appears on nothing else" on his mother's death notice is one of these two and the notice does not say which. ark:/61903/1:1:623r-9mm9 and 1:1:62gj-sd8z.. **the entry was read at the page on 9 october 2026** - film 008147497, item 4, *graaff-reinet. baptism records 1861-1866*, image 190, entry 79. **"gedoopt 29 sept. 1861"**: willem frederik thomas, ouders john barry and margaret welhelmina kolbe. **the date is his baptism and the register gives him no birth date**, where the entries either side of him both carry one. **and the witnesses explain the place.** get: **petrus jacobus joubert, catharine maria sophia kolbe, ralph peter thomas, maria magdalena pretorius** - the second is his mother's own sister, standing beside a joubert as a married couple does. **so this font is not evidence that the household moved back to graaff-reinet**; it is evidence that a child was christened where its aunt was. **and the third witness is where his third name comes from**: ralph peter thomas, at the font of william frederick thomas barry

s: 2 Aug 1847, baptised Fauresmith 12 Mar 1848 – 23 Apr 1941, Meriba, district Bloemfontein — aged 93 · Kolbe
q: williem johannes kolbe of panfontein 2 aug 1847, baptised fauresmith 12 mar 1848 - 23 apr 1941, meriba, district bloemfontein - aged 93 · kolbe **12 october 2026 - and the day of his death was here too.** this record carried "1941 - aged about 94" while the timeline already gave **23 april 1941, at meriba in the district of bloemfontein**, from his **civil death registration**. born 2 august 1847, he was **93**, not about 94. the registration is also the strongest thing this archive has for the identification, and it was not read for that: it enters him **born 1848 at philippolis**, which is the birthplace the afrikaans sources give for the general - **arrived at independently by a registrar who had never read them**. the year loses to his own baptism entry; the place is the corroboration. the conflation flagged below is therefore better supported than it was, and still not proved by a document naming the two together. **27 september 2026 - a baptism register names his parents, and corrects his birthday.** *south africa, free state dutch reformed church records*, familysearch 1:1:q2hl-bycg: **willem johannes kolbe, born 2 august 1847, baptised at fauresmith on 12 march 1848, entry number 18**, son of **john kolbe** and **anna jacoba van der merwe**. **the pedigree that was nienaber's is now a register's** - this archive had his parents at one remove, from a wikipedia article citing a 1947 dictionary whose page had never been seen, and the font has now said the same thing. **the date is not the same, and the date is the point.** the dictionary gives **9 july 1847 in the district of philippolis**; the register gives **2 august 1847** and baptises him at **fauresmith**. a register entered within seven months of the birth beats a dictionary compiled a century later, so this archive now carries 2 august - and a discrepancy of four weeks in a life otherwise agreed to the year is worth leaving visible rather than tidying away. **what is still not proved** is that the child baptised at fauresmith is the general: the register makes a willem johannes kolbe, born 1847 to this couple; the prisoner list makes a williem johannes kolbe, aged 54 in 1901, at panfontein in the bloemfontein district; the dictionary makes a general born 1847 who died in 1941. **three documents and one year** - and no single paper yet carries the career and the font together. **and he took church membership at bloemfontein on 2 august 1869, his own twenty-second birthday**, on the same day as his brother john henry. **and his death is in a civil register, with philippolis on it.** *south africa, orange free state, civil death registration*: **willem johannes kolbe, died 23 april 1941 at meriba, bloemfontein**, born **1848** at **philippolis, orange free state**. **the 1941 is the dictionary's 1941 and the philippolis is the dictionary's philippolis**, arrived at from a government register that never read the dictionary - which is the strongest thing yet said for the prisoner, the general and the baptised child being one man. the **1848** is an age at death and loses to the font's 2 august 1847. **he married christina cath petronella pretorius on 8 may 1880** in the free state, aged thirty-two. taken prisoner in 1901, aged 54, at panfontein in the bloemfontein district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 603. sent to natal. **and on 21 september 2026 the line in the prisoner list got a life.** he is **general willem johannes kolbe (1847-1941)**, who led the **bloemfontein commando** and commanded the southern districts of bloemfontein. **born 9 july 1847 in the district of philippolis** - the place his grandfather preached at, and where charles bell drew a kolbe in the pulpit in 1834. he was at the **siege of kimberley, where he was made general**, and afterwards at **paardeberg, driefontein and the brandwaterkom**, and he rode in **de wet's invasion of the cape colony in february 1901** - the year he was captured. **two horses were shot under him.** the french general de villebois-mareuil spoke of his leadership with praise; he was liked in his commando and is said to have treated the burghers kindly. **the source is printed, not a tree** - but read at one remove, and that is said plainly. the career above is in *afrikanergeskiedenis* (petronel fourie) and on the afrikaans wikipedia. **the pedigree below is on the wikipedia article only**, which cites **p. j. nienaber, *afrikaanse biografiese woordeboek* (voortrekkerpers, 1947), p. 139** and the fourie piece without saying which carries what; the fourie piece was read here in full and has no genealogy in it at all, **so nienaber is the source by elimination and his page has not been seen**. **and it names his house.** father **j. g. e. kolbe**, mother **anna jacoba van der merwe**, grandfather **george augustus kolbe, "a german missionary"**, grandmother **margaret downing**, the grandfather at **knapdaar, burgersdorp**, the home farm **onder-leeuwberg in the bloemfontein district**, and the father **a commandant in the basuto war of 1865**. every one of those is held here already and independently, including the two women's names and the farm the commandant died on. **the 1847 in the prisoner list and the 1847 in the dictionary are the same year, and panfontein and onder-leeuwberg are the same district.** **what is still not proved**: that the man in the prisoner list is the man in the dictionary. two documents agreeing on a name, a year and a district is strong and is not a register. **vab mhg m777**, the widow's 1896 estate, would name all twelve children - and so, in his own words, might *herinneringe van genl. w j kolbe* at the free state archives.

dordrecht town · wodehouse where this side of the family married, and where its in-laws lived. hercules johannes mountjoy married maria sophia van niekerk here on 8 october 1888, aged 22 - a year before the 1889 font at barkly oost. james john mountjoy and maria louisa bertha kumm gave dordrecht as their place of last marriage too, on two death notices filed at barkly east fifty years later. and it is where maria sophia's mother died, at her own house, in december 1902. 

indwe colliery town · north-eastern cape a colliery town, and this archive took three passes to notice that the word matters. willem hermanus booyzen died at doorn street, indwe, on 13 september 1905 of an ulcer of the stomach. his daughter catharina maria sophia married joseph heinrich daschner here. and his son - a son this archive did not know it had - was confirmed here in 1907 at twenty-one, married here in 1908 as a mijnwerker of dugmore mijn, and had two children baptised here in 1908 and 1910, both entered onecht. their grandmother kathleen barry stood godmother at the first font, three years after she was widowed in this town. indwe is where the family testimony's last line turns out to be true, in the wrong province. 

lady grey town · north-eastern cape he is entered as a boer - farmer - of lady grey at his marriage in 1879, and a mason at his death in 1905. something took the land away in between, and the 1884 estate says it may already have been gone. ladygreytownnortheasterncapeheisenteredasaboerfarmerofladygreyathismarriagein1879andamasonathisdeathin1905somethingtookthelandawayinbetweenandthe1884estatesaysitmayalreadyhavebeengone

colesberg town · northern cape midlands george augustus kolbe, the 1820 settler, died on the farm "wurtemburg" in this district on 1 december 1844. his widow signed the death notice here in january 1845, and the 1840 montjoy notice was signed here too. and he was there before the town was. john montgomery, founder of burgersdorp, writing in the friend of the free state in 1869 about a journey made about 1824, passed "by koolskop, where the father of the late lamented commandant kolbe conducted a bushmen mission school, and which is now colesberg". colesberg was laid out in 1830. if montgomery is right - and he is recalling forty-five years back, and names the man only as the father of a commandant who had died the year before - then the settler was keeping a mission school for bushmen on this ground six years before there was a town on it, and twenty years before he died in the district.

german savoy church church · strand, london where johan gottlieb kolbe was actually buried on 26 november 1845, entry 55, grave 7 - not st john the baptist, leamington, warwickshire, as the tree has it. the correction makes the family more coherent, not less: they are german lutherans of the savoy. the registers are at the national archives, series rg 4 - deaths and burials in rg 4/4625, 4626, 4628 and 4631, births and baptisms in rg 4/4627 and 4629. the 1845 burial entry this archive cites sits in one of those four, and can now be checked against the original rather than taken on trust.

marico district · western transvaal a substantial booyzen farming district - and this archive can no longer say whose. seven booyzen claims for compensation as burghers were filed here in 1903-04, and the booyzen children who died in the johannesburg and vereeniging camps came from farms in this district. this entry used to call them "emphatically someone else's". that judgement rested on the belief that this family was in the cape until about 1907 - and the 1876 sterfkennis at rustenburg, one district east, shows it was not. no document links this family to any of the seven claims. no document rules it out either. unresolved is the honest word. 13 september 2026: and now a documented booysen marriage in the district. hendrik stephanus booysen - seventh child on the 1876 sterfkennis, son of the direct ancestor - married charlotta elizabetha dormehl at zeerust, the principal town of marico. it still links this family to none of the seven compensation claims. it does mean the last of the three districts has had one of these people standing in it, and the sentence this archive withdrew was wronger than it knew. 15 september 2026: the seven claims were pulled in full and the index line is the whole record - no farm, no forename, no amount. the same search turned up something nobody asked for: a jgl booyzen countersigning the subsidy application, the book orders and all four quarterly returns of a farm school at kwaggafontein in this district, 1898-1899. he is not identified. he is a candidate for the jan gerhardus lodewicus born 4 december 1855, of whom this archive has said for months that nothing is known. 

kwaggafontein farm · district marico, transvaal a farm with a school on it, and the whole of its correspondence with the government survives. forty-eight files in tab source od, from 4 october 1897, when g.e. ter haar of kafferskraal asked for a teacher, to april 1900, when the teacher asked for his money to be sent to the landdrost and the war closed the file. the teacher was h. de vries, fetched by wagon in december 1897. a jgl booyzen is on eight of the forty-eight - the subsidy application, the book orders, all four quarterly returns, the explanation of a £61-6-0 deficit, and a letter of may 1899 arguing that £8 too little subsidy had been paid. he is the school's money man, and he is not identified.

booysens suburb, johannesburg · witwatersrand not a family place - a trap. booysens is a mining suburb south of the johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from forest hill and kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. it means every name-index search for booysen in johannesburg returns people whose only connection to the word is an address. the archive met it head-on: a death notice indexed under the surname daschner turned out to belong to charles bruce rennie, a miner of booysens, and nothing else about him touches this family at all. 

brakfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal the farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. on 14 september 1876, thirteen days after the death, somebody at brakfontein filled in sterfkennis no. 678 for petrus jacobus booijsen, aged 88, and wrote the names of his parents on line 3. fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 may 1891 and their son five days after her. and in 1892 hendrik stefanus, marrying again at zeerust, still gives brakfontein as his home - sixteen years on the same ground. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. 

lichtenburg district · western transvaal where this family's western transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - fifth of the eight children on the 1876 sterfkennis, born district graaff-reinet about 1818 - died on the farm vaalbank in this district on 25 may 1885, estate tab mhg o/2899. his daughter magdalena susanna maria died on the same farm on 1 may 1920, and her sterfkennis names him. lichtenburg is one district west of rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of marico. 

dugmore mine colliery · indwe, district wodehouse where a booyzen worked underground. the indwe marriage register of 21 september 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as "dugmore mijn" and the groom's trade as "mijnwerker". it is the only mine anywhere in this archive attached to a named member of this family, and it is coal in the cape rather than gold on the rand. the coordinates are approximate - the workings were at indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed. 

vaalbank farm · district lichtenburg, transvaal one farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - born district graaff-reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 sterfkennis - died here on 25 may 1885. his daughter magdalena susanna maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 may 1920. it is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached johannesburg. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. and a school on it. the education files of the south african republic hold a school at vaalbank, district lichtenburg, post office rietkuil, teacher j.p. louw, running through 1898 and 1899 - and the man beside the teacher on its money papers is written ds. booysen and ds booijsen. in february 1899 he wrote to the government to ask how school materials could be provided to orphans, arising from a case among them. whether ds. is a david schalk or the dutch abbreviation for a minister cannot be read off an index line, and six weeks earlier the same school wrote "ds van roojen" in the same slot. 

cherryville farm · district barkly east the third named barry farm, after manorowen and jerpoint. harriet louisa barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 september 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to manorowen to be buried. her father, who signed the form, gave his own residence as manorowen - so cherryville is somewhere the family worked rather than lived, or another barry household entirely. the coordinates are approximate. 

slang river locality · north-eastern cape where dorothea regina barry, daughter of hendrik nicholaas barry and anna johanna maria schoeman, was baptised on 3 april 1892. from the index rather than the register, and placed only approximately. slangriverlocalitynortheasterncapewheredorotheareginabarrydaughterofhendriknicholaasbarryandannajohannamariaschoemanwasbaptisedon3april1892fromtheindexratherthantheregisterandplacedonlyapproximately

koedoesfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal where hendrik stephanus booysen died on 11 may 1908, aged seventy-nine, in the house of his son-in-law willem grobelaar. a farmer with no movable property, some land, and mutual wills with both of his dead wives. thirty-two years earlier he had signed his own father's sterfkennis at brakfontein, one district over. the coordinates are approximate. 

zeerust town, district marico · transvaal the principal town of marico, and the district this archive spent weeks holding at arm's length with the sentence "they are not this family, who were cape". hendrik stefanus booijzen married here on 14 april 1892 - 63, a widower of brakfontein - and signed his second wife's death notice here in august 1902. the sentence is withdrawn.

q: driefontein farm, groot marico · district marico, transvaal charlotta elizabeth dormehl's own place. she gave it as her home when she married at zeerust in april 1892, and she died there on 6 february 1902 - three months before the peace, and ten years into a marriage to a man who farmed a hundred miles away at brakfontein. she never moved to him. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not placed. 

zwartruggens town · transvaal where diederik arnoldus booysen was born about august 1887 and lived as a karweier - a transport rider. his 1935 sterfkennis is the first document in this archive printed in afrikaans rather than dutch or english, and it names his parents: ockert johannes stephanus booysen and elizabeth johanna sophia myburgh, both by then dead. zwartruggenstowntransvaalwherediederikarnoldusbooysenwasbornaboutaugust1887andlivedasakarweieratransportriderhis1935sterfkennisisthefirstdocumentinthisarchiveprintedinafrikaansratherthandutchorenglishanditnameshisparentsockertjohannesstephanusbooysenandelizabethjohannasophiamyburghbothbythendead

klerksdorp town · transvaal where ockert johannes stephanus booysen died on 16 january 1921, aged 69 - the man who signed his father's death notice in 1908 and who carried his mother's father's name out of the district of cradock and into the western transvaal. it is a civil registration and it names no parents, which is why this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse. he has no estate file of his own. 

market street, pretoria street · pretoria, transvaal elizabetha margaretha booijzen, born marais, died in a zinc building in market street on 1 june 1900 - the capital's main street, four days before lord roberts entered the town. her husband david schalk booijzen, the direct ancestor's brother, did not file her death notice for three years and nine months, and against the question about movable property he wrote "none. compensation claim filed." 

turffontein suburb · johannesburg, transvaal 18 anderson street. richard peter booyzen, twenty-four, married, a sawyer, died here of influenza and pneumonia on 25 october 1918 after eleven days - the centre of black october, which killed some fourteen thousand people on the rand in six weeks. he was buried at brixton two days later. his birthplace on the form is the cape of good hope: born in the north-eastern cape, dead in a johannesburg mining suburb at twenty-four. 

mayfair suburb · johannesburg, transvaal this archive has had mayfair as a word on two pages and never as an address. kathleen barry died here in 1940. her great-granddaughter catherine mary sophia booyzen was married at st joseph's, mayfair on 15 january 1949 - the hinge into the lerena archive. and her son henry james booyzen was living at 3 15th avenue when he died in 1956. three generations in one suburb, and the cemetery register is what finally gave it a street number. 

roodepoort town · west rand, transvaal hendrik stephanus nicolaas booysen - baptised at rustenburg in 1882, dead at kempton park in 1959 - was buried in the central cemetery of the municipality of roodepoort-maraisburg on 12 october 1959, section i d.r., entry 96. this archive published him as buried at johannesburg for an afternoon because the familysearch collection carries that title for every register inside it. 

goedehoop place · pretoria, transvaal two men of this story lived here. charles petrus barend lowies, a hawker born in the district of cradock about october 1848, is "of goedehoop, pretoria" on his 1905 death notice - he died in the pretoria lunatic asylum on 5 june that year, leaving twelve children, six still minors. and david schalk booijzen, born in the district of cradock in june 1848, gives goede hoop, pretoria as his home on the register when he marries lowies's widow on 27 november, five months and twenty-two days later. this archive read that register first and wrote the address down without knowing what it meant. coordinates approximate. 

s: Hill, place of capture · Eastern Transvaal
q: tolosberg hill, place of capture · eastern transvaal where three booyzens were taken, and the only place on this map whose position this archive cannot vouch for. stefanus francois, petrus jacobus and david schalk booysen - prisoners 18463, 18464 and 18465, all of pretoria and all of the pretoria commando - were captured here on 25 april 1901, among forty-two boers taken with two guns and much stock. six weeks later they sailed from cape town on the city of cambridge. the hill itself is not on any map this archive has found. it is in no gazetteer reachable by search, in no battle list, and in no day-by-day war diary of 1901; the single source for the name gives only "tolosberg in the waterval valley, eastern transvaal". the pin is therefore placed at waterval boven, in the elands river valley - the waterval valley of the eastern transvaal, and twenty kilometres from dalmanutha, where the same man had fought the previous august. that placement is this archive's inference and not the source's. there is more than one waterval in the transvaal, including one in the lydenburg district north of here, and the hill could as easily be there. jeppe's map of 1899 has now been read and it does not carry the name. sheet 6 of the six-sheet map - the definitive survey of the south african republic, finished the year the war began - was examined over about twenty-five kilometres of the elands river valley either side of this pin, at full resolution. it names every farm with its number: waterval 161, kindergoed, elandshoek, eerste geluk, groot geluk, nooitgedacht, vlakplaats, kaalbosch, schoonspruit, kietspruit, weltevreden, treurfontein, uitkomst - and waterval boven and waterval onder stations on the delagoa bay line, with godwaan station east of them. it also names hills, in the form jeppe used: mauch bg., spitskop, tafel kop, peerds kop, zwart kop, zuikerboschkop, silverkop, vaalkop. there is no tolosberg among them. that does not move the pin and it does not prove the source wrong; it means the name was local, or was spelt otherwise, or was never a surveyed feature. the pin is still an inference - but it is now a tested one. 

knap daar farm · district colesberg the kolbe farm before wurtemburg. a land memorial of 1839 - cape town archives repository, lg 552, reference 664 - records "reverend g kolbe" asking that government ground adjoining his farm knap daar, in the district of colesberg, be surveyed and auctioned. this archive has george augustus kolbe dying at the farm wurtemburg in the same district on 1 december 1844, and knows he preached across the orange river; the memorial styles him reverend five years earlier and gives him land. the identification rests on an initial and a district, not on a full name, and the pin is placed at colesberg because the farm itself is not on any map read here. 

wakkerstroom town and district · eastern transvaal where the settler's family ended up, four hundred miles from the font. george augustus kolbe the 1820 settler died at colesberg in 1844 and is buried at burgersdorp; his son frederik fortunatus baptised eight children at colesberg, hopetown and bethulie between 1863 and 1881; and three of those eight marry or are found at wakkerstroom in the eastern transvaal. the eldest, another george augustus, was born at colesberg on 29 july 1863 and died here on 28 september 1954, aged ninety-one - a man whose life spans the whole of this archive's south african century. two men named george augustus kolbe lived and are buried here, born two years apart - 2 october 1861 and 29 july 1863 - and the older of them was the prisoner of war of 1902. two of his sons died here in 1918 four months apart, which is the influenza, and one of them carried the london surname downing into the eastern transvaal, which is what proved the connection. a woman named angeline kolbe died here on 15 november 1900, aged 28, and this archive cannot say who she was. 

s: Town, and a camp · Eastern Transvaal
q: volksrust town, and a camp · eastern transvaal twenty miles from wakkerstroom, on the natal border. frederik fortunatus downing kolbe married here. this archive also put a child's grave here for half a day and has taken it back: martha angeline kolbe, sixty days old, is buried at wakkerstroom, and the index that said volksrust was naming the district, which wakkerstroom lies inside. volksrust held one of the concentration camps, and the naairs index holds a camp grave for a g.e. kolbe, aged 35 - which is not the angeline kolbe who died at wakkerstroom in 1900, a different age in a different year in a different town. no person in this archive is yet shown to have been in that camp. 

s: Town, capital of the Orange Free State · Orange Free State
q: bloemfontein town, capital of the orange free state · orange free state the town the commandant's whole public life was attached to, and it took this archive until today to give it a pin. john gerson eliezar kolbe was a director of the bloemfontein bank, a justice of the peace, commandant of this district and a deacon of its dutch reformed church; he advertised a lost promissory note for £154 sterling on its market square in march 1864; he sat as foreman of the jury in a forgery trial here in 1866, before mr van soelen. his farm lay about two hours' ride away. and the man the free state estate index hides his widow behind was this town's own landdrost. francis mccabe, born at a frontier military post on 29 september 1817, son of dr patrick mccabe of the british army on the cape frontier, married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 and was dead by 23 february 1872, of heart disease on the modder river road after a cart went into a sluit in the moonlight. he was buried here on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried from the house by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred people walking behind. and a death in this district, added 13 october 2026. willem johannes kolbe - the panfontein prisoner this archive argues is general w. j. kolbe - died at meriba in this district on 23 april 1941, aged 93, by his civil death registration. that registration is also the best thing the identification has: it enters him born 1848 at philippolis, which is the birthplace the afrikaans sources give for the general, reached independently by a registrar who had never read them. meriba itself is not plotted - no coordinate has been established for it, and none is invented here, so the fact sits at the district town until the farm can be located. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: philippolis mission station, later town · southern orange free state where the settler's children grew up, on the word of a man writing in 1868 who knew them. the obituary of commandant john gerson eliezar kolbe says his father "became a missionary to the griquas at philippolis, and most of his family, we believe, grew up there". this archive had reached the same conclusion from the children's baptism places - harriet hachilah machilah born here in 1831 - and this is a fourth, independent source for it. philippolis was the london missionary society's griqua station; george augustus kolbe was an l.m.s. missionary. and there is a picture of it. on dr andrew smith's expedition charles bell painted a church service here with kolbe preaching - catalogued as the original at museumafrica and as a photographic copy at the university of edinburgh, cswc 60 item 3. neither has been seen, and it would be the only likeness of anybody in this archive born before 1850. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: bethulie mission station, later town · southern orange free state and the family was here eleven years earlier than this entry used to say. the station was boesmanskool when george augustus kolbe was placed at it, among the san, with james clark. he gives the date himself in a letter printed in the society's monthly for 1831: "when i arrived, in april, 1828, with my colleague, in the bushman country", having resided "nearly three years among the bushmen previous to my removal to this station". clark says it from the other side, writing from the bushman station on 31 december 1828: "brother kolbe and myself removed to this station, and arrived here in the beginning of may last." added 13 october 2026 - until then this place began the kolbe story at 1839, because the 1828 evidence was only found on 11 october. the other mission on the circuit, and a font this family came back to. frederik fortunatus kolbe was born here in 1839 - the source of a forename that has since crossed into four surnames - and johan casimir in 1844, the year his father died. forty-two years later frederik fortunatus brought his own youngest daughter, adriana henrietta johanna, back to be baptised here on 23 october 1881.

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: leeuwberg farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state where commandant kolbe died, on the night of friday 3 april 1868, of typhus caught on commando. the pin was at fauresmith and it was wrong. it rested on a 1903 free state land file recording a "leeuwberg no 465, dist. faurismith" - a farm of the right name in the right province thirty-five years later, and nothing more - and it was published with its own objection attached, that fauresmith is a hundred and thirty kilometres from kaalspruit while the obituary says he died at the one and lies at the other. the objection has been answered against the pin. the friend of the free state of 13 january 1870 advertises for sale "the farm, wildebeestkooi, adjoining the farm leeuberg, the property of the late j.g.e. kolbe, about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". fifteen or twenty kilometres, not a hundred and thirty. the fauresmith farm is a different farm of the same name, and the two-farm contradiction this archive could not reconcile was never a contradiction - leeuberg and kaalspruit are neighbours. a man named jephts, described by the court as a man of colour, was living here in 1868 and owned a chestnut riding horse; it was stolen with two of the family's, and his name is in the record beside theirs. **27 september 2026 - the farm is now a residence and not only a deathbed.** two free state civil marriage entries name it as where people lived: the commandant's widow in **july 1871**, and **jan hendrik kolbe, veeboer, with his bride** in **june 1872**, hers written "dito" under his. **that is three documents on one farm in four years** and the strongest reason yet to think the bloemfontein-district leeuwberg, not the fauresmith one, is the place. **the pin is still not moved on it**, because a residence in a register names a farm and not a coordinate. 

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: kaalspruit farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state his own address, in his own advertisement. the friend of the free state, 9 march 1864: a lost promissory note, £154 sterling, signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit". the obituary of 1868 says he settled here about 1850 and lies buried here. the pin is at bloemfontein and it is an inference: a free state soil-conservation district is registered as "kaalspruit - kafferrivier (bloemfontein)", which pairs the same two names the advertisement pairs, in the district whose bank he was a director of and whose paper he advertised in. a name pair is not a survey beacon. the friend's own transcriber read this farm as "[randspruit]", bracketed and doubtful; the advertisement is why this archive reads kaalspruit. 15 september 2026 - the guess now has three documents behind it. the obituary of his second wife's husband calls him "the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", the town being bloemfontein. an 1870 auction advertisement puts the neighbouring farm leeuberg "about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". and his widow was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868. kafferberg, kaalspruit, leeuberg, wildebeestkooi and springfield are one neighbourhood, and it is not at fauresmith.

hoopstad town · orange river colony where the werdmuller line ends up. charles andrew werdmuller - second son of the man who married the settler's fourth daughter - is "charles werdmuller, j.p. of hoopstad" by 1909. his wife charlotte anne, born callaghan, died here on 17 february 1891 aged thirty-two, "after a long illness", having arrived "only a few months ago, in rather indifferent health", of a disorder of the heart that proved organic. she left "a husband and two little girls", and one of those girls married a holder of the victoria cross.
